BURHAN:v3p329/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p329/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p329/r3.claim: The shift to “We adorned” draws attention to the doctrine that the stars adorn and guard the lowest heaven, against those who denied it.
BURHAN:v3p329/r3.anchor: فعدل عن الغيبة في قضاهن وأوحى إلى التكلم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p61/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p61/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p61/r5.claim: The organized world testifies to one powerful, wise, merciful God rather than a plaything or battleground of multiple gods; those distracted by alleged intercessors await doom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p61/r5.anchor: this world is not the product of a merry maker or the play field or battle field of various gods

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r1.claim: After describing the earth, the passage turns to heaven; “He turned toward heaven” means He directed His will to creating it, without implying physical influence elsewhere.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r1.anchor: ثم استوى إلى السماء: أي قصد إليها وتوجه دون إرادة تأثير في غيرها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r2.claim: The apparent account says heaven’s original material was smoke; a report from the Jewish Torah says heat over water raised foam and smoke, from which earth and heavens were made.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن المادة التي خلقت منها السماء كانت دخانا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya supplies omitted verbs for making, perfecting, and completing the heavens and earth before the command to come.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية: هنا لفظ متروك يدل عليه الظاهر، وتقديره: فأوجدها وأتقنها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers literal speech after God grants heaven and earth life and perception; he acknowledges that others take their response figuratively.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r4.anchor: ورجح قول من ذهب إلى أنهما نطقتا نطقا حقيقيا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r5.claim: Zamakhshari understands the command and their compliance as depicting their nonresistance to God’s creative will, not an actual exchange of speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r5.anchor: والغرض تصوير أثر قدرته في المقدورات لا غير، من غير أن يحقق شيء من الخطاب والجواب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r6.claim: To explain why earth is addressed although created earlier, Zamakhshari distinguishes creating its body from spreading it after the heaven, citing the earth’s later spreading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r6.anchor: قد خلق جرم الأرض أولا غير مدحوة، ثم دحاها بعد خلق السماء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation makes “come” mean assume the form and function God intends: earth as a settled dwelling and heaven as a roof.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r7.anchor: ائت يا أرض مدحوة قرارا ومهادا لأهلك، وائت يا سماء مقببة سقفا لهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r8.claim: He also allows the two to be commanded to meet each other in the complementary arrangement intended by wisdom.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p288#2/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: لتأت كل واحدة صاحبتها الإتيان الذي أريده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r1.claim: Zamakhshari reads “willingly or unwillingly” as an image for the inescapable effect of divine power and parses both words as circumstantial accusatives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r1.anchor: هو مثل للزوم تأثير قدرته فيهما، وأن امتناعهما من تأثير قدرته محال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r2.claim: He explains the masculine plural طائعين by treating heaven and earth as speakers and responders, comparable to other masculine plurals used of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r2.anchor: لما جعلت مخاطبات ومجيبات، ووصفت بالطوع والكره، قيل: طائعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r3.claim: They read أتيا and أتينا as forms from “to give,” meaning heaven and earth yielded their obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد: أتيا على وزن فعلا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes this reading to mean that heaven and earth gave God the obedience He sought.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r4.anchor: وذلك بمعنى أعطيا من أنفسكما من الطاعة ما أردته منكما،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r5.claim: Zamakhshari instead derives the reading from mutual agreement: each was to comply with the other, and both agreed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r5.anchor: أنه جعل هذه القراءة من المواتاة، وهي الموافقة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r6.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r6.claim: Al-Razi also derives the long-vowel reading from agreement and says it means they hastened to comply; taking it as “give” would require an awkward omitted object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r6.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون من الإيتاء الذي هو الإعطاء لبعد حذف مفعوله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r7.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r7.claim: Al-A‘mash reads كرها with a ḍamma, a dialect variant; the author says the form more often means hardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: أو كرها بضم الكاف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya suggests “they said” refers to the plural groups of heavens and earth, expressed as singulars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقوله قالتا، أراد الفرقتين المذكورتين:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r9.claim: The author rejects Ibn Atiyya’s account: the text previously mentioned one heaven and one earth, so a natural dual is appropriate; the cited poem is a different construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p289/r9.anchor: هذا وليس كما ذكر، لأنه إنما تقدم ذكر الأرض مفردة والسماء مفرد لحسن التعبير عنهما بالتثنية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r3.claim: A further objection says the command to come signifies creation, so addressing an already created earth as if to create it is impossible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r3.anchor: فلو سبق إيجاد الأرض على إيجاد السماء لاقتضى إيجاد الموجود بأمره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r4.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r4.claim: Muqatil says heaven was created before earth and treats the sequence marker as if an omitted “had been” were understood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r4.anchor: ونقل الواحدي في البسيط عن مقاتل أنه قال: خلق الله السماء قبل الأرض،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r5.claim: Al-Razi rejects combining ثم’s sequence with a past “had been,” since that would make the wording contradictory.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: فقدر ثم كان قد استوى جمع بين ضدين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r6.claim: Al-Razi nevertheless prefers heaven-first chronology by interpreting creation as divine decree or determination rather than immediate bringing into existence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p290/r6.anchor: والمختار عندي أن يقال: خلق السماء مقدم على خلق الأرض.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r2.claim: The discourse uses ثم because heaven’s creation is the more wondrous sign, much like report-ordering in other verses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r2.anchor: ولما كان خلق السماء أبدع في القدرة من خلق الأرض، ألف الأخبار فيه بثم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r3.claim: The command to heaven and earth depicts the realization of God’s previously described creative will, as speech can illustrate praise already given.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r3.anchor: فهذا تصوير لما أثنيت به وتفسير له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r5.claim: “He fashioned them as seven heavens” may parse سبع as a circumstantial accusative, a second object, or a specification of an ambiguous pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p291/r5.anchor: فقضاهن سبع سماوات: أي صنعهن وأوجدهن،

BIQAI-FULL:v6p141#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p141#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p141#2/r1.claim: The cosmos’ refusal and awe mean each part delivers what God deposited in it at the appointed time, like the creatures’ ‘we come willingly’ response.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p141#2/r1.anchor: أتينا طائعين , والحاصل أنه جعلت الإرادة وهي الأمر التكويني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p690/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p690/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p690/r1.claim: The author condemns an ignorant distorter who assigned “they said” to al-Khiḍr, mistaking a more remote figurative reading for better and more miraculous expression.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p690/r1.anchor: كان يجعل الضمير للخضر ؛ لأن ما كان فيه من آفة الجهل وسقم الفهم

RAZI-FULL:v18p173/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p173/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p173/r3.claim: Fāṭir does not by itself mean creation from absolute nothing: the heavens were made from smoke, humans from clay, and producing a form from existing matter does not entail creating that matter.
RAZI-FULL:v18p173/r3.anchor: إلا أن الحق أنه لا يدل عليه ويدل عليه وجوه

NAHHAS:v4p51/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p51/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p51/r1.claim: The source says this event occurred on Thursday, when God addressed the heaven and earth with the command to come willingly or unwillingly.
NAHHAS:v4p51/r1.anchor: قالوا في يوم الخميس ( فقال لها وللأرض أئتيا طوعا أو كرها )

NAHHAS:v4p51/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p51/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
NAHHAS:v4p51/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads the command as a call to give obedience.
NAHHAS:v4p51/r2.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير أنه قرأ ( ائتيا طوعا أو كرها ) أي أعطيا الطاعة

NAHHAS:v4p51/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p51/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p51/r3.claim: The verse uses the masculine plural طائعين after the feminine pair said they came; al-Kisai offers three explanations: it includes their inhabitants, treats them as rational after their coming, or fits the verse ending.
NAHHAS:v4p51/r3.anchor: وقرأ ( قالتا أتينا طائعين ) ولم يقل طائعات ففي هذا ثلاثة أجوبة للكسائي

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r23.speaker: Other commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r23.claim: Rejecting the symbolic reading as contrary to the plain text, they say God temporarily gave the particles intellect, hearing, and speech, as with the heavens and earth; bodily organs also testify.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r23.anchor: Others, however, reject this interpretation as against the plain meaning of the text

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r5.claim: طوعاً means willingly and spontaneously, whereas طائعاً means obedient to God's will.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r5.anchor: (طوعاً) تعني تلقائياً من النفس و (طائعاً) تعني طائعاً لإرادة الله سبحانه وتعالى

RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r1.claim: Maqatil, as transmitted by al-Wahidi, says the heavens were created before earth and reads ثم as indicating that God had already turned to heaven, with an implied كان.
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r1.anchor: ونقل الواحدي في ( البسيط ) عن مقاتل أنه قال : خلق الله السموات قبل الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r2.claim: Al-Razi calls Maqatil's construction weak: ثم implies succession while كان implies anteriority, so the combined wording is contradictory.
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r2.anchor: هو عندي ضعيف ، لأن تقدير الكلام ثم كان قد استوى إلى السماء ، وهذا جمع بين الضدين

RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r3.claim: Because the command to come occurred before heaven and earth existed, it cannot be a literal command or legal charge; Al-Razi directs readers to his prior explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r3.anchor: امتنع حمل قوله { * ئتيا } على الأمر والتكليف ، فوجب حمله على ما ذكرناه

RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r4.claim: The wording displays God's complete power: heaven and earth must come whether they wish to or refuse, like a ruler commanding a subordinate.
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r4.anchor: الجواب : المقصود منه إظهار كمال القدرة والتقدير : ائتي شئتما ذلك أو أبيتما

RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r5.claim: طوعا and كرها are accusatives of state, meaning willingly or under compulsion.
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r5.anchor: وانتصابهما على الحال بمعنى طائعين أو مكرهين

RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r6.claim: Their answer says they came willingly, not unwillingly.
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r6.anchor: { قالتا أتينا } على الطوع لا على الكره

RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r7.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r7.claim: One reported interpretation assigns willingness to heaven and compulsion to earth: heaven moves in obedient regularity, its inhabitants obey, and its qualities are superior, whereas earth varies and is dark and dense.
RAZI-FULL:v27p91#2/r7.anchor: وقيل إنه تعالى ذكر السماء والأرض ثم ذكر الطوع والكر ، فوجب أن يتصرف الطوع إلى السماء

RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r1.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r1.claim: A group takes the command literally: God gave heaven and earth life, understanding, and capacity to obey, as He makes mountains and human limbs speak.
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r1.anchor: قال القائلون بهذا القول وهذا غير مستبعد ، ألا ترى أنه تعالى أمر الجبال أن تنطق

RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r2.claim: Supporters argue that the apparent meaning stands absent an obstacle, the rational plural suggests awareness, and the rejected Trust shows creation can know God and receive commands.
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r2.anchor: الأصل حمل اللفظ على ظاهره إلا إذا منع منه مانع ، وههنا لا مانع

RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r3.claim: Al-Razi objects that the command means coming into existence; at that moment heaven and earth were nonexistent and could neither understand nor receive an order.
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r3.anchor: المراد من قوله { ائتيا طوعا أو كرها } الإتيان إلى الوجود والحدوث والحصول

RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report transmitted through Mujahid, says God told heaven to bring out its sun, moon, and stars, and earth to split its rivers and bring forth its fruits, which had been deposited there.
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r4.anchor: روى مجاهد عن ابن عباس أنه قال : قال سبحانه للسموات أطلعي شمسك وقمرك ونجومك

RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r5.claim: Al-Razi rejects the deposited-things interpretation: 41:12 says God then completed the seven heavens, so their coming into being followed the command rather than preceding it.
RAZI-FULL:v27p93#2/r5.anchor: وذلك يدل على أن حدوث المسوات إنما حصل بعد قوله { ائتيا طوعا أو كرها }

RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r3.claim: Qāla may describe nonverbal expression: poets make birds, eyes, and a full water trough “speak,” as do the Qurʾānic commands to creation to say “Be” and to heaven and earth to come.
RAZI-FULL:v1p27#2/r3.anchor: لفظ قال قد يستعمل في غير النطق

STUDYQURAN:41:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:11/r1.claim: Istawā is rendered “turned to” here, while it is also rendered “mounted” in descriptions of God’s relation to the Throne.
STUDYQURAN:41:11/r1.anchor: Turned to renders the verb istawā, which is also translated “mounted”when employed in relation to God’s Throne

STUDYQURAN:41:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:11/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:11/r2.claim: Following the earth’s creation, God turned His attention to creating the heavens, as also indicated in 2:29.
STUDYQURAN:41:11/r2.anchor: in this context, as in 2:29, it means that after creating the earth God turned His attention to the creation of the heavens

STUDYQURAN:41:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:11/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:11/r3.claim: The heavens and earth’s willing response signifies that all things obey and submit to God.
STUDYQURAN:41:11/r3.anchor: That the heavens and the earth agreed to come willingly indicates that all things are obedient and subservient to God

TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r1.claim: God commands the sky to bring forth the sun, moon, and stars, and the earth to produce trees, fruit, plants, and rivers; both comply with what He created in them.
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r1.anchor: عن سليمان بن موسى، عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس، {فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين}

TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God told the heavens to reveal the sun, moon, and stars, and the earth to split its rivers and bring out fruit; they said they came obediently.
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r2.anchor: عن سليمان بن موسى، عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس، {فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين}

TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Tawus, glosses both commands and replies with أعطيا and أعطينا, meaning give and we gave.
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r3.anchor: عن طاوس، عن ابن عباس، في قوله {ائتيا} [فصلت: 11] «أعطيا» وفي قوله: {قالتا أتينا} [فصلت: 11] قالتا: «أعطينا»

TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r4.claim: The masculine plural طائعين follows the alif and nun of أتينا, whose first-person plural pronoun matches the form used by male speakers.
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r4.anchor: لأن النون والألف اللتين هما كناية أسمائهما في قوله {أتينا} [فصلت: 11] نظيره كناية أسماء المخبرين من الرجال عن أنفسهم

TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r5.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r5.claim: Some Arab grammarians explain the masculine plural as referring to the heavens, earth, and those within them.
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r5.anchor: كان بعض أهل العربية يقول: ذهب به إلى السموات والأرض ومن فيهن

TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r6.claim: Other grammarians say the masculine form was used because the sky and earth, by speaking, resembled male human beings.
TAB-FULL:v20p391#2/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون منهم: قيل ذلك كذلك لأنهما لما تكلمتا أشبهتا الذكور من بني آدم

BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r1.claim: After explaining creation’s determination, the passage explains how it was brought about; attention to the earth and human livelihood first invites the addressees to faith and restrains disbelief and transgression.
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r1.anchor: شروع في بيان كيفية التكوين إثر بيان كيفية التقدير

BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r2.claim: ثم marks the ordered transition to the next stage and also signals special care in originating the higher realms.
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r2.anchor: وفي ثم إظهار كمال العناية بإبداع

BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r3.claim: Though استوى ordinarily means becoming straight and even, it means to intend and turn toward here, since its bodily literal sense cannot apply to God.
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r3.anchor: والاستواء ضد الاعوجاج من قولهم استوى العود إذا اعتدل واستقام حمل في هذا المقام على معنى القصد والتوجه

BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r4.claim: God directed His will toward the heaven in a straight, undivided intention, without intending another creation comparable to it.
BURSEVI:v8p179#2/r4.anchor: ثم قصد نحو السماء بإرادته ومشيئته قصدا سويا وتوجه إليه توجها لا يلوي على غيره

BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r1.claim: The waw is circumstantial and its feminine pronoun refers to the heaven; دخان is smoke, described as fine terrestrial particles lifted by heat.

BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib’s lexicon describes smoke as smoke accompanying flame, and vapor as moist water-particles rising in air with rays reflected from water surfaces.
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r2.anchor: الدخان العثان المستصحب للهب والبخار أجزاء مائية رطبة

BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r3.claim: The heaven was a dark, smoke-like substance; calling it heaven anticipates its eventual state, and the comparison indicates it had no cohesion.
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r3.anchor: أمر ظلماني يعد كالدخان ، وهو المرتفع من النار

BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib reads ‘it is like smoke’ as indicating that the early heaven had no solidity.

BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r5.claim: ‘Smoke’ may denote the heaven’s matter and bodily form or its minute constituent parts; their darkness was the obscurity before illumination, and their scattered, unconnected state resembled smoke.
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r5.anchor: عبر بالدخان عن مادة السماء يعني : الهيولى والصورة الجسمية

BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r6.claim: Another view is that the heaven was vapor rising from water, shaped like smoke, as in al-Kāshifī’s commentary.

BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r7.claim: In a report answering Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq, Ibn ʿAbbās says the Throne was first created over water; fire made the water cast up froth for the earth, and its vapor became heaven before the earth was spread, its mountains fixed, and provisions, plants, animals, and rivers made.
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r7.anchor: هذا جواب عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما لنافع بن الأزرق الحروري

BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r8.claim: The creation account distinguishes the earth’s initial creation from its later spreading and the subsequent setting of mountains and provision, citing ‘the earth after that He spread out.’
BURSEVI:v8p179#3/r8.anchor: بعد خلق السماء لذلك قال الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v8p180/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p180/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p180/r1.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to heaven; the earth is the one whose existence and contents had been determined.
BURSEVI:v8p180/r1.anchor: فقال لها} : أي للسماء ، {وللأرض} التي قدر وجودها ووجود ما فيها

BURSEVI:v8p180/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p180/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p180/r2.claim: The command means ‘come into being’: each realm is to exist in its appointed form and at its appointed time.
BURSEVI:v8p180/r2.anchor: كونا واحدثا على وجه معين ، وفي وقت مقدر

BURSEVI:v8p180/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p180/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p180/r3.claim: The command represents God’s effective will bringing heaven and earth into existence after their determination; there was no literal commander or commanded, only an analogy to an obeyed command.
BURSEVI:v8p180/r3.anchor: من غير أن يكون هناك آمر ومأمور كما في قوله : كن

BURSEVI:v8p180/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p180/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p180/r4.claim: طوعا and كرها are verbal nouns functioning as circumstantial expressions: willingly or unwillingly.

BURSEVI:v8p180/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p180/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p180/r5.claim: Whether they wished it or not, the image signifies that God’s power must take effect and cannot be resisted; it does not attribute rational will or choice to inanimate heaven and earth.
BURSEVI:v8p180/r5.anchor: وهو تمثيل لتحتم تأثير قدرته تعالى فيهما

TABATABAI:41:10-11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r7.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib says istiwāʾ with ʿalā means prevailing, while with ilā it means reaching or directing toward.
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r7.anchor: على ما ذكره الراغب - إذا عدي بعلى أفاد معنى الاستيلاء

TABATABAI:41:10-11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r8.claim: God turned toward heaven intending its creation, not by spatial movement, which is impossible for Him.
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r8.anchor: أي توجه إليها وقصدها بالخلق دون القصد المكاني الذي لا يتم إلا بانتقال القاصد من مكان إلى مكان

TABATABAI:41:10-11/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r9.claim: One view takes “then” as delay in the account rather than actual existence, citing the statement that earth was spread after heaven was built.
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r9.anchor: لكن قيل إن { ثم } لإفادة التراخي بحسب الخبر لا بحسب الوجود والتحقق

TABATABAI:41:10-11/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r10.claim: Tabatabai argues that spreading the spherical earth is its formation, and the earth details in both passages match; the explicit “after that” in 79 is more temporal than “then,” so “then” here is non-temporal.
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r10.anchor: والاعتراض عليه بأن مفاده تأخر دحو الأرض عن بناء السماء ودحوها غير خلقها مدفوع بأن الأرض كروية فليس دحوها وبسطها غير تسويتها كرة

TABATABAI:41:10-11/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r11.claim: “While it was smoke” describes heaven’s undifferentiated material state before it was formed as seven heavens, explaining the singular “heaven.”
TABATABAI:41:10-11/r11.anchor: وقوله { وهي دخان } حال من السماء أي استوى إلى السماء بالخلق حال كونها شيئا سماه الله دخانا

TABATABAI:41:11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:11/r1.claim: The address follows God’s turning to heaven and is a creative command like “Be,” not an ordinary instruction.
TABATABAI:41:11/r1.anchor: فقوله لها وللأرض { ائتيا طوعا أو كرها } كلمة إيجاد وأمر تكويني كقوله لشيء أراد وجوده كن

TABATABAI:41:11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:11/r2.claim: The address and reply portray creation in familiar language and reflect that knowledge pervades beings and each is addressed suitably; further discussion is promised at 41:21.
TABATABAI:41:11/r2.anchor: ومجموع قوله لهما { ائتيا } الخ وقولهما له { أتينا } الخ تمثيل لصفة الإيجاد والتكوين على الفهم الساذج العرفي

TABATABAI:41:11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:11/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:41:11/r3.claim: Some say “come” means display existing effects and benefits; Tabatabai rejects it because their coming-to-be follows afterward.
TABATABAI:41:11/r3.anchor: وقول بعضهم إن المراد بقوله { ائتيا } الخ أمرهما بإظهار ما فيهما من الآثار والمنافع دون الأمر بأن توجدا

TABATABAI:41:11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:11/r4.claim: The wording requires both to come while presenting willingness and reluctance as alternatives.
TABATABAI:41:11/r4.anchor: وفي قوله { ائتيا طوعا أو كرها } إيجاب الإتيان عليهما وتخييرهما

TABATABAI:41:11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:11/r5.claim: Perhaps willingness or reluctance means prior readiness or its absence: their coming is unavoidable and their answer expresses inherent acceptance.
TABATABAI:41:11/r5.anchor: ولعل المراد بالطوع والكره - وهما بوجه قبول الفعل ونوع ملاءمة وعدمه - هو الاستعداد

TABATABAI:41:11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:11/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:41:11/r6.claim: Some take willingness or reluctance as a mere illustration of divine power, without attributing either state to them; Tabatabai rejects this because they reply that they came willingly.
TABATABAI:41:11/r6.anchor: وقول بعضهم إن قوله { طوعا أو كرها } تمثيل لتحتم تأثير قدرته تعالى فيهما واستحالة امتناعهما

TABATABAI:41:11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:11/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:11/r7.claim: The plural masculine “obedient” is used because address and reply are characteristic of rational beings.
TABATABAI:41:11/r7.anchor: والتعبير باللفظ الخاص بأولي العقل - طائعين - لمكان المخاطبة والجواب

TABATABAI:41:11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:11/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:11/r8.claim: The plural rather than dual may express humility: heaven and earth count themselves with God’s obedient creatures and answer on their behalf, as in al-Fātiḥa.
TABATABAI:41:11/r8.anchor: والتعبير بلفظ الجمع دون أن تقولا أتينا طائعتين لعله تواضع منهما بعد أنفسهما

TABATABAI:41:11-12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:11-12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:11-12/r1.claim: Including earth in the address after its creation and governance hints at a connection between earth and heaven; actions and reactions circulate among the visible world’s parts.
TABATABAI:41:11-12/r1.anchor: ثم إن تشريك الأرض مع السماء في خطاب { ائتيا } الخ مع ذكر خلقها وتدبير أمرها قبلا

TABATABAI:41:11-12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:11-12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:11-12/r2.claim: “Then He turned” signals sequence in discourse, not necessarily temporal delay.
TABATABAI:41:11-12/r2.anchor: وفي قوله { فقال لها وللأرض } تلويح على أي حال إلى كون { ثم } في قوله { ثم استوى }

TABRISI:41:11-12/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:11-12/r1.claim: Ṭawʿan and karhan are verbal nouns used as circumstantial accusatives, meaning obediently or reluctantly; ṭāʾiʿīn is also a circumstantial accusative.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r1.anchor: طوعا وكرها مصدران وضعا موضع الحال التقدير ائتيا تطيعان إطاعة

TABRISI:41:11-12/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:11-12/r3.claim: God then directed Himself to creating the heaven, which was smoke.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r3.anchor: أي ثم قصد إلى خلق السماء وكانت السماء دخانا

TABRISI:41:11-12/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:41:11-12/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the smoke was vapor from the earth.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كانت بخار الأرض

TABRISI:41:11-12/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:11-12/r5.claim: The basic sense of istiwāʾ is straightness and direction toward arranging matters properly.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r5.anchor: وأصل الاستواء الاستقامة والقصد للتدبير المستقيم تسوية له

TABRISI:41:11-12/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:41:11-12/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan offers the alternative that God's command turned toward the heaven.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r6.anchor: وقيل: معناه ثم استوى أمره إلى السماء عن الحسن

TABRISI:41:11-12/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:41:11-12/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the heaven came with the sun, moon, and stars, while the earth came with its rivers, trees, and fruits.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أتت السماء بما فيها من الشمس والقمر والنجوم

TABRISI:41:11-12/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:11-12/r8.claim: The command and reply are not literal speech: God reports creating heaven and earth without difficulty, as though an order were instantly obeyed.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r8.anchor: ليس هناك أمر بالقول على الحقيقة ولا جواب لذلك القول بل أخبر الله سبحانه عن اختراعه السماوات والأرض

TABRISI:41:11-12/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:11-12/r9.claim: The creation-without-delay image is like God's command that when He wills something, He says Be, and it is.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r9.anchor: إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

TABRISI:41:11-12/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r10.speaker: قطرب
TABRISI:41:11-12/r10.claim: Qutrub says the masculine plural means the heavens and earth came bringing the rational beings within them, whose grammatical gender prevails.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r10.anchor: لأن المعنى أتينا بمن فينا من العقلاء فغلب حكم العقلاء عن قطرب

TABRISI:41:11-12/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:41:11-12/r11.claim: Another explanation says they were addressed as rational speakers, so the reply uses the rational plural, as in 21:33.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r11.anchor: وقيل: إنه لما خوطبن خطاب من يعقل جمعن جمع من يعقل

TABRISI:41:11-12/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:11-12/r12.claim: An anonymous poetic example has an animal addressed with humanlike perception and praise, illustrating speech that treats a nonhuman as rational.

TABRISI:41:11-12/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:11-12/r13.claim: A second anonymous poem addresses a ruin as if it could speak, another example of attributing rational speech to something nonhuman.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r13.anchor: وقال آخر: ألا أنعم صباحا أيها الرسم وانطق

TABRISI:41:11-12/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:11-12/r14.claim: This wording indicates that heaven was created after earth and that earth's provisions were created before it was spread out.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r14.anchor: يفيد أنه خلق السماء بعد الأرض وخلق الأقوات فيها

TABRISI:41:11-12/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:11-12/r15.claim: The later statement that earth was spread after that is reconciled by saying earth already existed but was not spread until after heaven was created.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r15.anchor: وعلى هذا فتكون الفائدة فيه أن الأرض كانت مخلوقة غير مدحوة

TABRISI:41:11-12/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:11-12/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:11-12/r16.claim: God first made heaven smoke, then layered it into seven heavens and adorned it with lamps to show His intrinsic power, knowledge, and independence while all else depends on Him.
TABRISI:41:11-12/r16.anchor: وإنما جعل الله السماء أولا دخانا ثم سماوات أطباقا ثم زينها بالمصابيح

THALABI:v8p287/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p287/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p287/r9.claim: Istiwa here means that God turned to and intended the creation and shaping of the heaven; most authorities classify this istiwa as an attribute of action.
THALABI:v8p287/r9.anchor: ثم استوى إلى السماء أي عمد إلى خلق السماء وقصد، تسويتها، والاستواء من صفة الأفعال على أكثر الأقوال،

THALABI:v8p287/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p287/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p287/r10.claim: The heaven's smoke was vapor from water.

THALABI:v8p287/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p287/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p287/r11.claim: God commands heaven and earth to bring out their stored benefits and reveal them for the welfare of His creatures.
THALABI:v8p287/r11.anchor: فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها أي جيئا بما خلقت فيكما من المنافع،

THALABI:v8p287/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p287/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p287/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas specifies that God told the heavens to bring forth the sun, moon, and stars, and the earth to open its rivers and produce its fruits.
THALABI:v8p287/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قال الله تعالى للسماوات: اطلعي شمسك وقمرك ونجومك، وقال للأرض: شقي أنهارك واخرجي ثمارك.

THALABI:v8p287/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p287/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p287/r13.claim: The plural masculine taʾiʿin is used because the address encompasses heaven, earth, and their inhabitants; they answer as rational beings.
THALABI:v8p287/r13.anchor: ولم يقل طائعتين، لأنه ذهب به إلى السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن، مجازه: أتينا بمن فينا طائعين

THALABI:v8p287/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p287/r14.speaker: أحد الأنبياء
THALABI:v8p287/r14.claim: An unnamed prophet asked what God would do if heaven and earth had disobeyed; God replied that He would command a creature to swallow them, and placed that creature within His knowledge.
THALABI:v8p287/r14.anchor: وبلغنا أن بعض الأنبياء، قال: يا رب لو إن السماوات والأرض حين قلت لهما ائتيا طوعا أو كرها عصيناك، ما كنت صانعا بهما؟

THALABI:v8p287/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p287/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p287/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the verbs with a long alif, meaning give obedience from yourselves; the two say that they have given it.
THALABI:v8p287/r15.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس: آتيا وآتينا بالمد، أي أعطينا الطاعة من أنفسكما. قالتا: أعطينا.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:11-14/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:11-14/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:11-14/r1.claim: Istawa here means to set out for or attend to the creation of the heaven, which was vapor rising from water.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:11-14/r1.anchor: قصد وعمد { إلى } خلق { السماء وهي دخان } بخار مرتفع عن الماء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:11-14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:11-14/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:11-14/r2.claim: God commands heaven and earth to produce their benefits for creation: the heavens' sun, moon, and stars, and the earth's water and fruit; both obey willingly.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:11-14/r2.anchor: بما خلقت فيكما من المنافع، وأخرجاها لمنافع خلقي

QASHANI:41:9-11/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:41:9-11/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:41:9-11/r3.claim: God's turning to create heaven marks the difference in perfection between the creations, and their different direction and substance, not temporal delay since time did not yet exist.
QASHANI:41:9-11/r3.anchor: قصد إلى إيجادها وثم للتفاوت بين الخلقين في الإحكام وعدمه

QASHANI:41:9-11/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:41:9-11/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:41:9-11/r4.claim: Heaven's smoke is a subtle substance, unlike dense, heavy earthly substances.
QASHANI:41:9-11/r4.anchor: جوهر لطيف بخلاف الجواهر الكثيفة الثقيلة الأرضية

QASHANI:41:9-11/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:41:9-11/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:41:9-11/r5.claim: God's command and will attached to bringing heaven and earth into existence, and both came immediately and obediently; this is figurative, since no actual speech occurred.
QASHANI:41:9-11/r5.anchor: تعلق أمره وإرادته بإيجادهما فوجدتا في الحال معا كالمأمور المطيع

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r1.claim: When istawā is joined to ilā, it means to take a straight direction or turn directly toward something.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r1.anchor: ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ kelimesi إِلَى ile sılalandığı zaman istikāmet almak, dosdoğru teveccüh etmek mânasınadır

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r2.claim: Regarding God, Elmalılı interprets the phrase as God's direct will and direction of divine care toward the heaven.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r2.anchor: Allah teâlâ hakkında doğrudan doğru irade ile tefsir olunur. Yani inâyet-i ilâhiyesini doğrudan semâya doğru tevcih buyurdu

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r3.claim: The command can mean that earth and heaven submit together whether or not it suits their natures, or that they come into existence.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r3.anchor: tabiatlarınıza gerek muvâfık olsun gerek olmasın, yahut ikiniz de vücûda gelin, tekevvün edin

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r4.speaker: Râzî ve Kadı Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r4.claim: Some commentators take thumma as rank-sequence rather than time: heaven was created before earth but described after its creation.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r4.anchor: Râzî ve Kadı Beyzâvî gibi müfessirînin bir kısmı zamânî değil, rütbî terâhî ile anlamışlar

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r5.speaker: Râzî ve Kadı Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r5.claim: On this reading, come means come into being, and smoke describes the first, still dark primordial matter.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r5.anchor: Bu surette ٱئْتِيَا demek “vücûda gelin” mânasına tekvinden ibarettir. “Duhan” da ilk maddenin yaratıldığı hâldir

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r6.claim: Elmalılı calls that reading good but objects that the circumstantial clause and preceding command risk implying the primordial matter is eternal.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r6.anchor: maddenin kıdemini îhâm etmek gibi bir şâibe vardır

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r7.speaker: ekser müfessirîn; author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r7.claim: Most commentators read thumma temporally: earth was first created before heaven, though its spreading came later as 79:30 states; Elmalılı prefers this majority reading.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r7.anchor: ekser müfessirîn ise ثُمَّ’nin terâhisi zamânî olduğuna kāil olmuşlar ve Arz’ın ilk halkı semâdan evvel olup ancak

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r8.claim: He takes heaven here to mean the region above earth, the air, as in other verses describing rain sent down from heaven.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r8.anchor: olduğu gibi Arz’ın yukarısı, yani hava tarafı demek olduğuna zâhib oluyorum

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r9.claim: On this account earth was initially fiery as it separated from heaven, and gases rose from that fire to form the smoky upper region.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r9.anchor: Arz ilk yaratılışında ibtidâ semâdan ayrıldığı sıra ateş hâlinde idi, sonra bu ateşten onun yukarısına doğru semâsı olarak duman hâlinde gazlar püskürüyordu

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r10.claim: God orders the smoky heaven and earth to move together in an ordered system, adjusting to one another whether their natures welcome it or not.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r10.anchor: kerhen gelin tabiatınıza uygun gelse de gelmese de ikiniz birlikte birbirinize uyarak bir nizam üzere hareket edin dedi

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r11.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r11.claim: Some commentators understand the command and willing response in a conscious, sentient sense.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r11.anchor: şu‘ûrî mânada anlamak istemişlerse de mutlak tevâfuk ve inkıyad mânasına olmak daha mütebâdirdir

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r12.claim: Elmalılı prefers the more immediate sense of complete concord and obedience rather than conscious speech.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r12.anchor: mutlak tevâfuk ve inkıyad mânasına olmak daha mütebâdirdir

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r13.claim: Created things accept even effects contrary to their ordinary nature as part of their nature, so no created thing disobeys divine command.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r13.anchor: Emr-i ilâhîye karşı hiçbir muhalefetleri vâki‘olmaz.

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r14.claim: He says the receptivity called the law of inertia can explain the natural-seeming events of all celestial and terrestrial bodies.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r14.anchor: Onun için “atâlet kanunu” denilen bu mutâva‘at ve kābiliyet ile bütün ecrâm-ı semâviye ve ecsâm-ı arziyenin hâdisâtı tabî‘î imiş gibi îzah olunabilir.

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r15.speaker: قِيل
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r15.claim: An unattributed account says the Throne rested on water before creation; heat produced curd and smoke, the curd became earth, and the rising smoke became heaven.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r15.anchor: Denilmiş ki semâvât ve Arz halk olunmadan Arş su üzerinde idi, sudaki suhûnetten bir kaymak ve bir duman çıktı

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r16.speaker: Fahr-i Râzî
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r16.claim: Razi says this account is absent from the Qur'an and appears at the beginning of what Jews call the Torah; it could be accepted if evidence supported it.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r16.anchor: Fahr-i Râzî der ki: “Bu kıssa Kur’an’da yoktur, Yehûd’un Tevrat dediği kitabın evvelinde vardır. Bir delil delâlet ederse kabul olunabilir.”

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r17.speaker: Zemahşerî
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r17.claim: Zamakhshari also transmits an unusual account in which dry land became earth and then split into two earths.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r17.anchor: Zemahşerî garib bir fıkra daha nakleder de kuraktan bir arz yaptı, sonra da onu ayırdı iki arz yaptı der

ELMALILI:41:11-13/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r18.claim: Elmalılı wonders whether Zamakhshari's two earths might mean the Moon separating from earth or the separation of America.
ELMALILI:41:11-13/r18.anchor: Ayrılan bu iki arz nedir? Ya Arz’dan Kamer’in ayrılması olacak, yahut da Amerika’nın ayrılması olacaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r1.claim: The verb i’tiyā, “come,” is figurative for God’s creative command bringing the heavens and earth into being, so the authors render it “come to the scene of existence”; duhān marks this as a cosmic creation command.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r1.anchor: “Geliniz” anlamındaki i’tiyâ fiili tefsirlerde göklerin ve yer kürenin yaratılmasını, oluşmasını (tekvîn) sağlayan ilâhî buyruk olarak mecazi anlamda yorumlanmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r2.claim: Duhān literally means smoke; exegetes have interpreted it as water vapor (for example, Shawkani).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r2.anchor: Sözlükte “duman” anlamına gelen duhân kelimesi tefsirlerde “su buharı” olarak yorumlanmıştır (meselâ bk. Şevkânî, IV, 581).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r3.claim: In light of scientific developments, Esed’s reading of duhān as hydrogen gas appears accurate according to current knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r3.anchor: bilimsel gelişmeler de dikkate alınarak söz konusu kelimenin hidrojen gazı olarak yorumlanması (Esed, III, 972) bugünkü bilgilere göre isabetli görünmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r4.claim: The previous two verses discuss earth’s creation and blessings, but verse 11 does not say earth was created before heaven; here thumma signals heaven’s greater importance rather than chronological sequence, so the authors translate it “moreover,” agreeing with Shawkani and Ibn Ashur.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r4.anchor: Şevkânî (IV, 582) ve İbn Âşûr’un da (XXIV, 245) haklı olarak belirttikleri gibi– bu bağlamda zaman yönünden sonralığı değil, semanın yaratılmasının, arzın yaratılmasına göre daha büyük bir önem taşıdığını göstermektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r5.claim: Because earth and heavens were not created at the same time, the command to come is understood as God saying “be, come into existence” to each when He willed to create it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r5.anchor: Esasen yerin ve göklerin yaratılması aynı anda olmadığı için ikisine “gelin, buyurdu” cümlesini, her birini yaratmayı murat ettiğinde, “ol, varlığa gel” dedi, onlar da var oldular, şeklinde anlamak gerekir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r6.claim: The statement that heaven and earth came obediently is also interpreted figuratively: God’s will and power apply absolutely to creation, and His command cannot fail to be fulfilled (Shawkani).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:11/r6.anchor: “Boyun eğerek geldik dediler” cümlesi, yaratılışın her alanında olduğu gibi göklerin ve yerin yaratılmasında da Allah’ın irade ve kudretinin mutlak sûrette geçerli olduğunu, buyruğunun gerçekleşmemesi diye bir durumun düşünülemeyeceğini ifade eden temsilî bir anlatım olarak da yorumlanmıştır (Şevkânî, IV, 581).

BURHAN:v3p305/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p305/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p305/r4.claim: The masculine plural describes the rational creatures within heaven and earth, with rational males determining the agreement.
BURHAN:v3p305/r4.anchor: إنما جمعهما جمع السلامة ولم يقل طائعين ولا طائعات لأنه أراد ائنيا بمن فيكم من الخلائق طائعين

BURHAN:v3p305/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p305/r5.speaker: بعض النحويين
BURHAN:v3p305/r5.claim: Some grammarians derive طائعين from طاعنا, meaning we yielded, rather than from أطاعنا; Arab usage includes a she-camel yielding willingly.
BURHAN:v3p305/r5.anchor: وإنما قال طائعين ولم يقل مطيعين

BURHAN:v2p246/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p246/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p246/r2.claim: The sky and earth answer in the masculine plural طائعين, though a feminine dual might be expected, because they are represented as speaking rational beings.
BURHAN:v2p246/r2.anchor: الثاني والعشرون خطاب الجمادات خطاب من يعقل

BURHAN:v2p246/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p246/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
BURHAN:v2p246/r3.claim: The two explanations are literal speech after God gave the bodies life and perception, or figurative speech for their manifested willing submission; Ibn Atiyya prefers literal speech because nothing rules it out and it better displays divine power.
BURHAN:v2p246/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية والآول أحسن لأنه لاشيء يدفعه والعبرة فيه أتم

BURHAN:v2p62/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p62/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p62/r4.claim: Although the account might seem to total eight days, the four days for earth's provisions include the initial two; the heavens were completed in two more, totaling six.
BURHAN:v2p62/r4.anchor: مع اليومين المتقدمين ولم يرد بذكر ( الأربعة ) غير ما تقدم ذكره

BURHAN:v2p80/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p80/r10.speaker: الفراء والأشعري وجماعة من أهل المعاني
BURHAN:v2p80/r10.claim: Zarkashi endorses interpreting istiwa as turning toward and undertaking creation of the throne, analogous to the wording about turning toward the smoky heaven in 41:11; he says this avoids both denial and anthropomorphism.
BURHAN:v2p80/r10.anchor: قال الأستاذ والصواب ما قاله الفراء ( 1 ) والأشعري ( 2 ) وجماعة من أهل المعاني

ITQAN:v3p104/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p104/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p104/r3.claim: The text also illustrates plural forms used for two: the heavens and earth say they came obedient, and other cited examples apply plural wording to a pair.
ITQAN:v3p104/r3.anchor: ومثال إطلاقه على المثنى ﴿ قالتا أتينا طائعين ﴾ ﴿ قالوا لا تخف خصمان

ITQAN:v3p72/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p72/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v3p72/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports a questioner bringing Ibn Abbas apparent conflicts about polytheists’ denial, questioning in the afterlife, the creation sequence, and the wording “was Allah.”
ITQAN:v3p72/r2.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق في تفسيره أنبأنا معمر عن رجل عن المنهال بن عمرو عن سعيد بن جبير قال جاء رجل إلى ابن عباس

ITQAN:v3p73/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p73/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p73/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas’s answers show that these passages differ by circumstance or meaning rather than contradicting one another; each was revealed as intended.
ITQAN:v3p73/r1.anchor: فما اختلف عليك من القرآن فهو يشبه ما ذكرت لك وإن الله لم ينزل شيئا إلا وقد أصاب الذي أراد

ITQAN:v3p73/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p73/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p73/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the earth was created before the heavens; the heaven was smoke and was formed into seven heavens in two days after the earth’s creation.
ITQAN:v3p73/r2.anchor: وأما قوله ﴿ خلق الأرض في يومين ﴾ فإن الأرض خلقت قبل السماء

ITQAN:v3p73/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p73/r5.speaker: الحاكم
ITQAN:v3p73/r5.claim: Al-Hakim transmitted the full Ibn Abbas report and authenticated it; Ibn Hajar says its original is also in an authenticated collection and groups its questions into four apparent discrepancies.
ITQAN:v3p73/r5.anchor: أخرجه بطوله الحاكم في المستدرك وصححه

ITQAN:v3p73/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p73/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p73/r8.claim: The report’s chronology distinguishes creating the earth in two days, forming the heavens in two, then spreading the earth and placing its mountains and other features in two more days.
ITQAN:v3p73/r8.anchor: وعن الثالث أنه بدأ خلق الأرض في يومين غير مدحوة ثم خلق السموات فسواهن في يومين ثم دحا الأرض بعد ذلك وجعل فيها الرواسي وغيرها في يومين

ITQAN:v3p91/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p91/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p91/r10.claim: The Qur’an can address inanimate things in the form used for rational beings, as in the command to heaven and earth.
ITQAN:v3p91/r10.anchor: خطاب الجمادات خطاب من يعقل نحو ﴿ فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها ﴾

ITQAN:v3p15/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p15/r1.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi report from Ibn Abbas that istawa means settled; al-Suyuti says that, if authentic, it requires reinterpretation because settlement suggests corporeality.
ITQAN:v3p15/r1.anchor: حكى مقاتل والكلبي عن ابن عباس

ITQAN:v3p15/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r2.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p15/r2.claim: Some interpret istawa as istawla, meaning took control.
ITQAN:v3p15/r2.anchor: ثانيها أن ( استوى ) بمعنى ( استولى ) ورد بوجهين

ITQAN:v3p15/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p15/r3.claim: The istawla interpretation is rejected because God already controls the two realms, Paradise, and Hell, making the Throne's specification pointless.
ITQAN:v3p15/r3.anchor: أحدهما أن الله تعالى مستول على الكونين والجنة والنار وأهلهما فأي فائدة في تخصيص العرش

ITQAN:v3p15/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p15/r4.claim: The istawla interpretation is also rejected because taking control implies prior opposition and victory, which is unbefitting of God.
ITQAN:v3p15/r4.anchor: والآخر أن الاستيلاء إنما يكون بعد قهر وغلبة والله سبحانه وتعالى منزه عن ذلك

ITQAN:v3p15/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r5.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
ITQAN:v3p15/r5.claim: Asked about istiwa, Ibn al-Aʿrabi says to affirm what God has reported; he rejects istawla because it is said only after overcoming an opponent.
ITQAN:v3p15/r5.anchor: أخرج اللالكائي في السنة عن ابن الأعرابي أنه سئل عن معنى

ITQAN:v3p15/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
ITQAN:v3p15/r6.claim: Abu Ubayd offers ascended as the meaning of istawa.
ITQAN:v3p15/r6.anchor: ثالثها أنه بمعنى صعد قاله أبو عبيد

ITQAN:v3p15/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p15/r7.claim: The ascension interpretation is rejected because God is transcendent above ascending.
ITQAN:v3p15/r7.anchor: ورد بأنه تعالى منزه عن الصعود أيضا

ITQAN:v3p15/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r8.speaker: إسماعيل الضرير
ITQAN:v3p15/r8.claim: Ismaʿil al-Darir proposes reading the phrase as al-Rahman rose, with the Throne as what He established.

ITQAN:v3p15/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p15/r9.claim: The proposal is rejected because it makes ʿala a verb though it is unanimously a preposition; a verb would be written ʿala with alif as in ʿala fi al-ard.
ITQAN:v3p15/r9.anchor: أحدهما أنه جعل ( على ) فعلا وهي حرف هنا بإتفاق فلو كانت فعلا لكتبت بالألف

ITQAN:v3p15/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p15/r10.claim: The same proposal requires al-ʿarsh to be nominative, but no canonical reader recites it with that case.
ITQAN:v3p15/r10.anchor: والآخر أنه رفع ( العرش ) ولم يرفعه أحد من القراء

ITQAN:v3p15/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r11.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p15/r11.claim: A further reading ends the sentence at on the Throne and begins a new clause, He established what is in the heavens and earth.
ITQAN:v3p15/r11.anchor: أن الكلام تم عند قوله ﴿ الرحمن على العرش ﴾ ثم ابتدأ

ITQAN:v3p15/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p15/r12.claim: Al-Suyuti rejects the clause break because it disrupts the verse's order and intended meaning, and says it cannot account for the wording in 20:5.
ITQAN:v3p15/r12.anchor: ورد بأنه يزيل الآية عن نظمها ومرادها

ITQAN:v3p15/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r13.speaker: الفراء والأشعري وجماعة أهل المعاني
ITQAN:v3p15/r13.claim: Al-Farraʾ, al-Ashʿari, and other specialists say istawa means turned toward or intended the creation of the Throne; Ismaʿil al-Darir calls this correct, by analogy with 41:11.
ITQAN:v3p15/r13.anchor: قاله الفراء والأشعري وجماعة أهل المعاني

ITQAN:v3p15/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r14.speaker: إسماعيل الضرير
ITQAN:v3p15/r14.claim: Ismaʿil al-Darir calls the intention-to-create interpretation the correct one.

ITQAN:v3p15/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r15.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p15/r15.claim: Al-Suyuti objects that this interpretation is unlikely because the word here takes ʿala; if it meant turning toward, it would take ila as in 41:11.
ITQAN:v3p15/r15.anchor: قلت يبعده تعديته بعلى ولو كان كما ذكروه لتعدى بإلى

ITQAN:v3p15/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p15/r16.speaker: ابن اللبان
ITQAN:v3p15/r16.claim: Ibn al-Labban interprets God's istiwa as establishing balance through justice, giving each created thing its proper measure by wisdom.
ITQAN:v3p15/r16.anchor: سابعها قال ابن اللبان الاستواء المنسوب إليه تعالى بمعنى اعتدل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r1.speaker: أبو تمام
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r1.claim: Abu Tammam explicitly names both sides of his image: delay is smoke, and the favor is fire.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r1.anchor: وإنما هو شيء يضعه الآن أبو تمام ويتحمله ويعمل في تصويره

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r2.claim: A metaphor may omit the compared subject only when convention has established the likeness, as with light and knowledge; a newly invented likeness must name both sides.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r2.anchor: اطراح ذكر المشبه والاقتصار على اسم المشبه به وتنزيله منزلته وإعطاءه الخلافة على المقصود إنما يصح إذا تقرر الشبه بين المقصود وبين ما تستعير اسمه له

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r3.claim: Phrases such as “I met a lion in him” are not metaphors in this account; the construction appears as an established identification, as in “you will meet the lion in him.”
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r3.anchor: فإنه مما لا وجه لتسميته استعارة ألا تراهم قالوا لئن لقيت فلانا ليلقينك منه الأسد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r4.claim: “The abode of eternity” does not compare Hell to a separate entity; it simply predicates that Hell is their dwelling and home.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p289/r4.anchor: أن النار شبهت بدار الخلد إذ ليس المعنى على تشبيه النار بشيء يسمى دار الخلد

DAMGHANI:v1p253/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r9.claim: Istawā ilā means to intend or turn toward, as God turns toward the heaven.
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r9.anchor: استوى بمعنى قصد وعمد قوله تعالى في سورة فصلت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r1.claim: Istiwāʾ may be complete, as when a matter is sound or two things equal, or incomplete and needing a complement; with ilā it means intend, with maʿa equal.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r1.anchor: الاستواء : يقال على ضربين ، أحدهما : تام ، والآخر : ناقص . فالتام مثل ، قولك استوى الأمر إذا استقام .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r2.claim: With ilā, istawā means to intend or turn toward, as in God’s directing Himself toward heaven.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r2.anchor: أحدها : العمد والقصد . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في فصلت ] : ﴿ ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r3.claim: A second sense is settling or coming to rest, as the ark settled on Mount al-Jūdī.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r3.anchor: والثاني : الاستقرار . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود : ﴿ واستوت على الجودي ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r4.claim: A third sense is riding or embarking, as when Noah’s companions boarded the ark and riders mounted their animals.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r4.anchor: والثالث : الركوب . ومنه قوله تعالى في المؤمنين : ﴿ فإذا استويت أنت ومن معك على الفلك ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r5.claim: Istiwāʾ can mean strength and maturity, as when Moses reached his full strength.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r5.anchor: والرابع : القوة والشدة . ومنه قوله تعالى في القصص : ﴿ ولما بلغ أشده واستوى ﴾ ، أي : قوي واشتد .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r6.claim: A fifth sense is similarity or equality; cited verses ask whether the blind and seeing are equal.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r6.anchor: الخامس : التشابه . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام [ : ﴿ قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r7.claim: The final sense is elevation, as in the statement that the Merciful rose over the Throne.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p152/r7.anchor: والسادس : العلو . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في طه ] : ^ ( الرحمن على العرش استوى ) ^

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p388#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p388#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p388#4/r1.claim: Istawā ilā means He turned or directed Himself toward it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p388#4/r1.anchor: {ثم استوى إلى السماء} أي عمد لها.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r3.claim: The earth was created first in two days; the heavens, then smoke, were made in two; afterward God spread and anchored the gathered earth and grew its plants in two, totaling six days.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r3.anchor: فابتدأ الخلق للأرض على ما في الآي الأول في يومين، ثم خلق السموات وكانت دخانا في يومين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r4.claim: “After that He spread it” does not mean that earth was first created then; daha means that He spread and extended it after its initial creation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r4.anchor: وإنما كان يجد الطاعن متعلقا ومقالا لو قال: والأرض بعد ذلك خلقها أو ابتدأها أو أنشأها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r5.claim: Mujāhid says “after that” here means “together with that,” noting that the Arabs can use “with” and “after” equivalently.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد : بعد ذلك في هذا الموضع

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r1.speaker: عثمان
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r1.claim: The objectors report that Uthman saw a grammatical error in the codex and said the Arabs would correct it with their tongues.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r1.anchor: ورويتم عن عثمان أنه نظر في المصحف فقال: أرى فيه لحنا وستقيمه العرب بألسنتها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.speaker: قالوا
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.claim: They argue that Fussilat places the earth's creation before the heavens, whereas al-Naziat appears to place the heaven's construction before the earth's spreading.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.anchor: وقال بعد ذلك: ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r2.speaker: العجاج
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r2.claim: Al-Ajjaj's verse about the earth uses وحي for making it settle, illustrating revelation as subjection or directing.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r2.anchor: وحي لها القرار فاستقرت أي: سخرها لأن تستقر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r6.claim: He rejects interpreting the address to heaven and earth as mere creation or Hell's speech as a report of capacity, asking why strained evasions are needed when scripture allows creatures to speak.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r6.anchor: وأما تأويلهم في قوله جل وعز للسماء والأرض

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r7.claim: God can make skins, hands, and feet speak, and can make mountains and birds praise; this supports taking the speech of heaven and earth as possible.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p74/r7.anchor: وما في نطق جهنم ونطق السماء والأرض من العجب؟ والله تبارك وتعالى ينطق الجلود، والأيدي، والأرجل

MAJAZ:v2p196/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p196/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p196/r3.claim: The speech attributed to the heavens and earth is a figure in which inanimate things, like animals, are described through actions modeled on human behavior.
MAJAZ:v2p196/r3.anchor: «قالتا أتينا طائعين» (11) هذا مجاز الموات والحيوان الذي يشبه تقدير فعله بفعل الآدميين..

MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r1.claim: He cites celestial bodies, sky and earth, idols, ants, and the senses as examples in a discussion of grammatical agreement for nonhuman referents.
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r1.anchor: رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين

MAJAZ:v1p10/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p10/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p10/r3.claim: A dual expression can be followed by a predicate in the plural form.
MAJAZ:v1p10/r3.anchor: ومن مجاز ما جاء من لفظ الإثنين، ثم جاء لفظ خبرهما على لفظ خبر الجميع

MAJAZ:v1p10/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p10/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p10/r7.claim: The author introduces a further construction in which reports about animals and inanimate things take the wording used for human reports.
MAJAZ:v1p10/r7.anchor: ومن مجاز ما جاء من لفظ خبر الحيوان والموات على لفظ خبر الناس قال

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r1.claim: Dukhān is smoke rising from fire and figuratively the vapor seen over earth in drought; the normal plurals are أدخنة for fewness and دخنان for abundance, while دواخن is anomalous, explained as a metaphorical plural of داخنة.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r1.anchor: والدخان: ما ارتفع من لهب النار، ويستعار لما يرى من بخار الأرض عند جدبها.

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r2.claim: Expected plurals are أدخنة for fewness and دخنان for abundance; the unusual دواخن is explained as a metaphorical plural of داخنة, like عثان and عواوثن.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r2.anchor: وقياس جمعه في القلة: أدخنة، وفي الكثرة: دخنان نحو غراب وأغربة وغربان، وشذوا في جمعه

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r3.claim: Describing the heaven as smoke is a visual simile: to the eye its appearance is like smoke.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r3.anchor: " وهي دخان " من باب التشبيه الصوري؛ لأن صورتها صورة الدخان في رأي العين.

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r4.claim: The common reading uses the imperative from أتى and the matching past أتى; Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Mujahid lengthen both forms, reading آتيا and آتينا.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد: " آتيا قالتا آتينا " بالمد فيهما.

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r5.speaker: الرازي والزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r5.claim: Al-Razi and al-Zamakhshari take the lengthened forms from mutual compliance: let each comply with what suits it; the forms are فاعلا and فاعلنا with one object omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r5.anchor: أحدهما: أنه من المؤاتاة، وهي الموافقة أي: ليوافق كل منكما الأخرى لما يليق بها، وإليه ذهب الرازي والزمخشري.

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r6.claim: An alternative derives them from giving: the heaven and earth give obedience from themselves, requiring two omitted objects; Abu al-Fadl al-Razi rejects it as an implausible double omission, as does al-Zamakhshari.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r6.anchor: فعلى الأول يكون قد حذف مفعولا، وعلى الثاني يكون قد حذف مفعولين إذ التقدير: أعطيا الطاعة من أنفسكما

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r7.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r7.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Razi prefers deriving the lengthened آتينا from mutual compliance, or haste, with one object omitted, rather than from giving with two objects omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r7.anchor: وقد منع أبو الفضل الرازي الوجه الثاني. فقال: " آتينا " بالمد على فاعلنا من المؤاتاة

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r8.claim: طوعا and كرها are verbal nouns used as circumstantial accusatives, meaning willingly or unwillingly.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r8.anchor: مصدران في موضع الحال أي: طائعتين أو مكرهتين.

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r9.speaker: الأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r9.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads كرها with ḍamma; the author notes that the issue was discussed under Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r9.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش " كرها " بالضم. وقد تقدم الكلام على ذلك في النساء.

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya takes the dual speakers as the two groups, the heavens and the earths, collectively described in singular form.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " أراد الفرقتين المذكورتين. جعل السماوات سماء، والأرضين أرضا،

SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r11.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r11.claim: The Sheikh rejects Ibn ʿAtiyya's reading because only singular heaven and earth were previously mentioned, so the dual is natural; the cited poem's plural ropes refer to a different sense.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11/r11.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وليس كما ذكر؛ لأنه لم يتقدم إلا ذكر الأرض مفردة والسماء مفردة،

SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r1.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r1.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says the masculine rational plural includes all beings in heaven and earth, rational and otherwise, with rational beings prevailing in agreement.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أن المراد: أتيا بمن فيهما من العقلاء وغيرهم، فلذلك غلب العقلاء على غيرهم، وهو رأي الكسائي.

SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that heaven and earth receive rational treatment in being addressed and reported speech, so they take the rational masculine plural; compare 12:4.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه لما عاملهما معاملة العقلاء في الإخبار عنهما والأمر لهما جمعا كجمعهم، كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r3.claim: The scholars disagree whether the dialogue between heaven and earth is literal or figurative, and, if figurative, whether it is representation or imaginative personification.
SAMIN-DURR:41:11#2/r3.anchor: وهل هذه المحاورة حقيقة أو مجاز؟ وإذا كانت مجازا فهل هو تمثيل أو تخييل؟ خلاف.

ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r8.claim: Istawā ilā means that God turned or directed Himself toward heaven.
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r8.anchor: معنى استوى عمد إلى السماء وقصد

ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r9.claim: Ṭāʾiʿīn is an accusative circumstantial expression; heaven and earth are treated like rational beings, explaining the masculine plural.
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r9.anchor: على الحال منصوب، وإنما قيل طائعين دون طائعات، لأنهن جرين مجرى ما يعقل

ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r10.claim: Alternatively, the words mean “we and those within us came obediently.”
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r10.anchor: وقد قيل (قالتا أتينا) أي، نحن ومن فينا طائعين

ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r11.claim: The command means to obey willingly or to be compelled to obey.
ZAJJAJ:v4p380/r11.anchor: بمنزلة أطيعا الطاعة أو تكرها إكراها

ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n11/r1.claim: When thumma joins parallel statements without a necessary time sequence, it functions as a simple conjunction and can be rendered "and".
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n11/r1.anchor: it has the function of a simple conjunction, and may be rendered as "and".

ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n12/r1.claim: Asad identifies dukhan as gas, evidently hydrogen, which physicists regard as the primal element from which material particles evolve.
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n12/r1.anchor: a gas - evidently hydrogen gas, which physicists regard as the primal element from which all material particles of the universe have evolved and still evolve

ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n12/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n12/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n12/r2.claim: For sama in its cosmic sense, Asad points to his note 20 on 2:29.
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n12/r2.anchor: For the meaning of the term sama ("sky" or "skies" or "heaven") in its cosmic connotation, see note 20 on 2:29.

ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n13/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n13/r1.claim: Zamakhshari explains the command and the skies' and earth's submission as an allegorical picture of God's will bringing them into being as He wished, illustrating the effect of His almighty power.
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n13/r1.anchor: Zamakhshari observes: "The meaning of God's command to the skies and the earth to 'come', and their submission [to His command] is this

ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n13/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n13/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n13/r2.claim: Zamakhshari calls "willingly or unwillingly" a figurative expression for the inevitability of God's almighty will.
ASAD-NOTES:41:11#n13/r2.anchor: Zamakshari adds: "If I am asked about the meaning of [the words] 'willingly or unwillingly', I say that it is a figurative expression

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p842/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p842/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p842/r1.claim: Al-karh with fatḥa means coercion imposed from outside, contrasted with voluntary action; the source illustrates it with forced inheritance, spending, and the address to heaven and earth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p842/r1.anchor: الكَره) - بفتح الكاف - هو ما يأتي من الخارج يقابله الطوع

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p68/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p68/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p68/r2.claim: Verses 9–12 direct attention to God’s power, providence, wisdom, and oneness in the heavens and earth; verse 12 summarizes the argument, which he will discuss verse by verse before summarizing and addressing objections.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p68/r2.anchor: This topic is spread over four verses.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p68/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p68/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p68/r3.claim: Reflection on the world rules out self-origination, mere amusement, or a battleground of rival gods; it points instead to the planning and wisdom of an all-powerful, all-knowing God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p68/r3.anchor: it has come into being on account of the planning and wisdom of the all powerful and all knowing God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p70/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p70/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p70/r8.claim: The expression istawā ilā means directing attention or intention toward something.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p70/r8.anchor: means to “to direct attention to that thing;” “to make an intention of that thing.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p70/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p70/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p70/r9.claim: After the earth's earlier stages, God turned His attention to the sky, which was then in cloud form.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p70/r9.anchor: after creating the earth in the afore-mentioned

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
