ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r1.claim: The sky's cloud was dust and vapor, or a nebula; it was still rudimentary, formed during the earth's initial two-day stage, and istawā refers to God's attention to completing it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r1.anchor: The cloud refers to dust and vapour particles or in scientific terms can be called nebula.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r2.claim: The sky and earth began to be created at the same time, so the question of which was created first is irrelevant.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r2.anchor: the creation of the sky and the earth began at the same time;

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r3.claim: Like a building, the sky and earth were created through integrated stages, with attention moving between unfinished parts; the analogy helps explain their complex construction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r3.anchor: similar was the case with bringing into being the sky and the earth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r4.claim: The Qur'an presents sky and earth together as a building, sometimes mentioning the sky first and sometimes the earth, reflecting the integrated process.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p71/r4.anchor: the Qur’ān has mentioned both of them together in the capacity of a building.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r1.claim: Ṭāʾiʿīn is appropriate only for living beings with intention; Islahi takes the sky and earth's spoken response as evidence of conscious utterance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r1.anchor: Now this word is only appropriate to be used by those who are living and possess intention.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r2.claim: The expression's style resembles Solomon's letter to the Queen of Sheba (27:31); Islahi rejects alternative interpretations as failures to recognize this linguistic style.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r2.anchor: is very similar to what Solomon (sws) wrote to the queen of Sheba:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r3.claim: Apparently nonliving things understand God's commands, answer and follow them, and knowingly worship and praise Him; our inability to hear them reflects our limited knowledge.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p72/r3.anchor: the objects of this world which we regard to be non-living and unintelligent understand the directives of their Lord

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r3.claim: Creation was gradual, wise, and purposeful, not mere entertainment; its elaborate order entails that a Day of Judgement will come.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r3.anchor: this world has been created very gradually and with great wisdom according to a specific plan.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r4.claim: The Creator has immeasurable power and knowledge, needed no help to create, and cannot be helped by anyone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r4.anchor: neither did He require anyone’s help nor is anyone capable enough to help Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r5.claim: Sky and earth are one building occupied by humanity; their harmony shows that the same God created and controls both, disproving separate rulers for roof and floor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p73/r5.anchor: the sky and the earth are like a building in which God has placed man.

NASHR:v1p156/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r2.claim: Shuʿba died in 193 AH, was born in 95, and was a major learned, practicing authority; near death he said he had completed 18,000 recitations in a corner of the room.
NASHR:v1p156/r2.anchor: (وتوفي) أبو بكر شعبة في جمادى الأولى سنة ثلاث وتسعين ومائة

NASHR:v1p156/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r3.claim: When his sister cried at his deathbed, Shuʿba asked why and pointed out the corner where he had completed 18,000 full recitations.
NASHR:v1p156/r3.anchor: ولما حضرته الوفاة بكت أخته فقال لها: ما يبكيك

NASHR:v1p156/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r4.claim: Hafs died in 180 AH according to the preferred date, was born in 90, knew Asim's reading best, and was Asim's stepson.
NASHR:v1p156/r4.anchor: (وتوفي) حفص سنة ثمانين ومائة على الصحيح ومولده سنة تسعين

NASHR:v1p156/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r5.speaker: يحيى بن معين وابن المنادي والذهبي
NASHR:v1p156/r5.claim: Yahya ibn Maʿin calls Hafs the sound transmission of Asim; Ibn al-Munadi praises his memory and precision, and al-Dhahabi rates him reliable in qirāʾāt despite his hadith status.
NASHR:v1p156/r5.anchor: قال يحيى بن معين: الرواية الصحيحة التي رويت من قراءة عاصم رواية حفص

NASHR:v1p156/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r6.claim: Yahya ibn Adam died in 203 AH and was a leading imam and hadith memorizer.
NASHR:v1p156/r6.anchor: (وتوفي يحيى بن آدم) في النصف من شهر ربيع الآخر سنة ثلاث ومائتين

NASHR:v1p156/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r7.claim: Al-Ulaymi died in 243 AH, was born in 105, and was a distinguished, reliable, precise reader with a sound reading.
NASHR:v1p156/r7.anchor: (وتوفي العليمي) سنة ثلاث وأربعين ومائتين ومولده خمس ومائة

NASHR:v1p156/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r8.claim: Shuʿayb died in 261 AH and was a skilled, trusted, knowledgeable, precise qāriʾ.
NASHR:v1p156/r8.anchor: (وتوفي شعيب) سنة إحدى وستين ومائتين، وكان مقرئا ضابطا عالما

NASHR:v1p156/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r9.claim: Abu Hamdun died around 240 AH and was a reliable, precise, upright transmitter and reader.
NASHR:v1p156/r9.anchor: (وتوفي أبو حمدون) في حدود سنة أربعين ومائتين وكان مقرئا ثقة

NASHR:v1p156/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r10.claim: Abu Bakr al-Wasiti died in 323 AH and was born in 218; people credited him with spreading al-Ulaymi's reading, al-Naqqash praised him, and he held Wāsiṭ's central mosque post for years with a high Asim-reading isnad.
NASHR:v1p156/r10.anchor: (وتوفي أبو بكر الواسطي) سنة ثلاث وعشرين وثلاثمائة ومولده ثمان عشرة

NASHR:v1p156/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r11.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r11.claim: Ibn Khaliʿ died in 356 AH and was a trusted, precise, established reading teacher.
NASHR:v1p156/r11.anchor: (وتوفي ابن خليع) في ذي القعدة سنة ست وخمسين وثلاثمائة

NASHR:v1p156/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r12.claim: Al-Razzaz died around 360 AH and was a recognized qāriʾ.
NASHR:v1p156/r12.anchor: (وتوفي الرزاز) في حدود سنة ستين وثلاثمائة، وكان مقرئا معروفا

NASHR:v1p156/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p156/r13.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p156/r13.claim: Ubayd ibn al-Sabbah died in 235 AH; al-Dani calls him one of Hafs's leading and most precise students, while al-Ashnani praises his piety and asceticism.
NASHR:v1p156/r13.anchor: (وتوفي عبيد بن الصباح) سنة خمس وثلاثين ومائتين، وكان مقرئا ضابطا صالحا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p184#6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p184#6/r1.speaker: عكرمة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p184#6/r1.claim: In a report from the Prophet, creation begins on Sunday: the earth and its provisions are made over Sunday through Wednesday, the heavens on Thursday and Friday, and Adam in Friday's final hours; nothing was created on Saturday, contrary to the Jews' claim. The report links God's denial to 50:38.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p184#6/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد عن عكرمة مولى ابن عباس قال سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في كم خلقت السماوات والأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r1.claim: Istawā ilā means to intend or turn toward a place without turning toward something else.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r1.anchor: أي قصد إليها وتوجه دون إرادة تأثير في غيرها من قولهم : استوى إلى مكان كذا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r2.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r2.claim: Al-Raghib says istawā with ʿalā means mastery, as in the Throne verse; with ilā it means reaching or turning toward something, physically or through governance, with this verse an instance of the latter.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r2.anchor: وذكر الراغب أن الاستواء متى عدي بعلى فبمعنى الاستيلاء كقوله تعالى : ( الرحمن على العرش استوى )

ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r3.claim: Some construe the wording as elliptical, supplying creation: He then turned to create the heaven.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r3.anchor: أن في الكلام مضافا محذوفا أي ثم استوى إلى خلق السماء

ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.claim: Smoke is a dark, primordial material from which the heavens were composed; al-Ālūsī rejects indivisible atoms on the strength of arguments against them.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r4.anchor: أمر ظلماني ولعله أريد به مادتها التي تركبت وأنا لا أقول بالجواهر الفردة لقوة الأدلة على نفيها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r5.claim: One cosmological report says the Throne was over water before creation; God heated the water, foam became earth, and rising smoke became the heavens.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : إن عرشه تعالى كان قبل خلق السماوات والأرض على الماء فأحدث الله تعالى في الماء سخونة فارتفع زبد ودخان

ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r6.claim: Another report begins with a red ruby that melted under the divine gaze into water, from which foam and smoke rose and creation followed.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : كان هناك ياقوتة حمراء فنظر سبحانه إليها بعين الجلال فذابت وصارت ماء فأزبد وارتفع منه دخان

ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r7.claim: The smoke did not derive from elemental fire: fire follows earth and may not yet have existed; even if it existed, no one claims the heavens formed from it. The philosophers’ celestial fire sphere is unreal, and meteors do not require it.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r7.anchor: فليس الدخان كائنا من النار التي هي إحدى العناصر لأنها من توابع الأرض ولم تكن موجودة غذ ذاك على قول

ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r8.claim: On one interpretation, the command means bringing out the benefits placed in heaven and earth, not their coming into existence; it is a command of subjugation, whose sequence must follow their preparation or the later summary.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p102#2/r8.anchor: بما خلقت فيكما من المنافع فليس المعنى على إتيان ذاتهما وإيجادهما بل إتيان ما فيهما مما ذكر بمعنى إظهاره

ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r1.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r1.claim: One proposed reordered construction places completion of the seven heavens before the command to heaven and earth; al-Ālūsī finds it less likely to invite dispute but contrary to the apparent order.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r1.anchor: وقال بعض : الكلام على التقديم والتأخير والأصل ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان

ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r2.claim: Another reading takes the command as an order to come into existence in a specified form and appointed time, making it a beginning of formation after the prior account of determination.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r2.anchor: أو كونا وإحداثا على وجه معين وفي وقت مقدر لكل منكما فالمراد إتيان ذاتهما وإيجادهما

ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r3.claim: This formation reading is the one advanced by the author of Irshād al-ʿaql al-salīm and offered by others as a possibility; detailing earth and its provisions first highlights care for future human livelihood and urges faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r3.anchor: وهذا الوجه هو الذي قدمه صاحب الإرشاد وذكره غيره احتمالا وجعل الأمر عبارة عن تعلق إرادته تعالى بوجودهما

ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r4.claim: On this reading, the command represents God’s effective will through analogy with Be; there is no actual commander and commanded party.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r4.anchor: وجعل الأمر عبارة عن تعلق إرادته تعالى بوجودهما تعلقا فعليا بطريق التمثيل من غير أن يكون هناك آمر ومأمور

ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r5.claim: Although both are addressed, heaven alone is named as the object of divine turning because the preceding account already specified the earth’s existence and contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r5.anchor: وخص الاستواء بالسماء مع أن الخطاب المترتب عليه متوجه إليهما معا اكتفاء بذكر تقدير الأرض وتقدير ما فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r6.claim: Willingly or unwillingly portrays the irresistible effect of divine power and the impossibility of resistance, not literal willingness or reluctance in the two entities.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r6.anchor: تمثيلا لتحتم تأثير قدرته تعالى فيهما واستحالة امتناعهما من ذلك لا إثبات الطوع والكره لهما

ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r7.claim: The two verbal nouns function adverbially, meaning obediently or reluctantly.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r7.anchor: وهما مصدران وقعا موقع الحال أي طائعتين أو كارهتين

ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r8.claim: Their reply portrays complete responsiveness to divine power and their coming to be as commanded; obedience also presents their form as governed by profound wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r8.anchor: تمثيلا لكمال تأثرهما عن القدرة الربانية وحصولهما كما أمرا به وتصويرا لكون وجودهما كما هما عليه جاريا على مقتضى الحكمة البالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r9.claim: The masculine sound plural is explained by their being addressed and answering; feminine agreement is unnecessary because their gender is grammatical only.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p103/r9.anchor: وقيل : ( طائعين ) يجمع المذكر السالم مع اختصاصه بالعقلاء باعتبار كونهما في معرض الخطاب والجواب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r1.claim: Istawā ilā al-samāʾ means that God turned to undertake the creation of the sky.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r1.anchor: {ثم استوى إلى السماء} أي: عمد إلى خلق السماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r2.anchor: {وهي دخان} وكان ذلك الدخان بخار الماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r3.claim: The command means to do what God orders, as in the expression 'do what is best.'
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r3.anchor: ائتيا ما آمركما أي: افعلاه، كما يقال: ائت ما هو الأحسن، أي: افعله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through Ṭāwūs, glosses iʾtiyā as 'give forth.'
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r4.anchor: وقال طاووس عن ابن عباس: ائتيا: أعطيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports God telling the sky to produce the sun, moon, and stars, and the earth to open its rivers and bring forth fruit and vegetation; He said to obey willingly or be compelled, and both obeyed willingly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r5.anchor: قال الله عز وجل: أما أنت يا سماء فأطلعي شمسك وقمرك ونجومك، وأنت يا أرض فشقي أنهارك وأخرجي ثمارك ونباتك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r6.claim: The dual feminine subjects take the masculine plural ṭāʾiʿīn because the meaning includes the heavens, earth, and those within them; it means they came with what they contain, obediently, and rational speech permits the human plural.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p165#2/r6.anchor: لأنه ذهب به إلى السموات والأرض ومن فيهن

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r1.claim: Istawā ilā means to direct oneself toward a place with undivided attention, as in ordinary Arabic usage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r1.anchor: قصد نحوها من قولهم استوى إلى مكان كذا إذا توجه إليه توجها لا يلوي على غيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r2.claim: Thumma marks the difference in rank between the two creations, not a time delay, since Earth was spread after that before its mountains were formed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن ثم لتفاوت ما بين الخلقتين لا للتراخي في المدة

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r3.claim: The sky's smoke is a dark substance, perhaps its material or the minute particles from which it was composed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r3.anchor: أمر ظلماني، ولعله أراد به مادتها أو الأجزاء المتصغرة التي كتب منها

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r4.claim: One explanation is that heaven and Earth are told to manifest the effects and varied beings placed within them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r4.anchor: بما خلقت فيكما من التأثير والتأثر وأبرزا ما أودعتكما من الأوضاع المختلفة والكائنات المتنوعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r5.claim: Alternatively, they are ordered to come into existence, with the earlier creation understood as determination or ordering by rank.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r5.anchor: في الوجود على أن الخلق السابق بمعنى التقدير أو الترتيب للرتبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r6.claim: Another possibility is that the sky's coming is its coming-to-be while Earth's coming is its becoming spread, though the author notes the difficulty of this view.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r6.anchor: أو الإخبار أو إتيان السماء حدوثها وإتيان الأرض أن تصير مدحوة، وقد عرفت ما فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r7.claim: A further account has each come to cooperate with the other in producing what God intends.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r7.anchor: أو لتأت كل منكما الأخرى في حدوث ما أريد توليده منكما

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r8.claim: The reading ataya, from mutual cooperation, supports the interpretation that heaven and Earth should agree in carrying out God's intention.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r8.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة «آتيا» في المؤاتاة أي لتوافق كل واحدة أختها فيما أردت منكما

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r9.claim: Whether they will or refuse, the wording displays God's complete power and the inevitability of His will; it does not attribute actual willingness or aversion to them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r9.anchor: شئتما ذلك أو أبيتما والمراد إظهار كمال قدرته ووجوب وقوع مراده لا إثبات الطوع والكره لهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r10.claim: The verbal nouns ṭawʿan and karhan function as circumstantial expressions.

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r11.claim: The reply most likely pictures God's power affecting the two and their inherent response, portraying them as a master obeyed by a servant, like Be, and it is.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r11.anchor: والأظهر أن المراد تصوير تأثير قدرته فيهما وتأثرهما بالذات عنها، وتمثيلهما بأمر المطاع وإجابة المطيع الطائع

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r12.claim: The masculine plural ṭāʾiʿīn follows semantic treatment of the two as addressed beings, as in the cited form sājidīn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:11/r12.anchor: وإنما قال طائعين على المعنى باعتبار كونهما مخاطبتين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r10.claim: Then marks the heavens' greater scale and importance than the earth, along with God's great care for them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r10.anchor: ولفظ الاستواء وحب الغاية الدال على عظيم العناية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r11.claim: He explains istawā ilā as directing an intentional purpose toward the heaven and bringing that purpose to completion.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r11.anchor: أي قصد قصدا هو القصد منتهيا قصده

BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r12.claim: The heaven was smoke, understood as water vapor and figuratively compared in appearance to smoke rising from fire; the actions of forming earth and completing heaven's benefits overlap.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r13.claim: The heaven preceded the earth in its smoky state; the counted periods overlap because the creative actions overlap.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p556/r13.anchor: فالسماء متقدمة في الدخانية على الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r1.claim: The heavens and earth must release their entrusted benefits, such as water, plants, and minerals, at their appointed times and proper measures, willingly or unwillingly under compulsion rather than legal obligation.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r1.anchor: في إخراج ما أودعتكما من الأمانة في أوقاتها وعلى ما ينبغي

BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r2.claim: The two respond that they and what they contain submit completely, neither withholding nor changing what God commands.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r2.anchor: أي في كل ما رسمته فينا لا نحمل من ذلك شيئا بل نبذله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r3.claim: The two are addressed and speak as rational beings; the masculine plural طائعين treats them together with the rational creatures within them.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r4.claim: The dual form of their reply does not require the address to have occurred simultaneously; God may have addressed them in succession.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r4.anchor: لا يدل على جمعه في الزمان

BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r5.claim: Their obedience is their delivery of the entrusted benefits, rather than their bearing that trust themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r5.anchor: وذلك هو بذلهما للأمانة , وعدم حملها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r14.claim: Creation unfolded over six days rather than an instant to refute the notion that God acts by nature rather than choice; six is a perfect number, its proper divisors summing to it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r14.anchor: لو خلقه في لمحة لكان ذلك شبهة لمن يقول

BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r15.claim: The earth's two periods, counted for its substance and benefits, allude to shirk as a doubling; the heavens' signs more clearly establish divine unity and their inhabitants did not incur that warning.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r15.anchor: ولم يكرر في السماء لأن آياتها أدل على التوحيد ولم يحصل من أهلها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r16.claim: That the greater, more intricate heavens were made in less time than the earth further demonstrates God's free choice through wondrous wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p557/r16.anchor: مع أنها أكبر جرما وأعجب صنعا وأتقن جسما

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3270#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3270#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3270#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command “come” as “give,” and the response “we came” as “we gave.”
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3270#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله ، عنهما في قوله : ائتيا قال : اعطيا وفي قوله : ائتيا اعطينا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r1.claim: Thumma marks rank ordering: creating the heavens is greater in rank, with more and greater worlds, while mentioning earth first gives due attention to both subjects.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r1.anchor: { ثم } للترتيب الرتبي ، وهي تدل على أن مضمون الجملة المعطوفة أهم مرتبة من مضمون الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r2.claim: The rank-ordering particle does not imply that God decided to create heaven only after completing earth, or that heaven was actually created later.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r2.anchor: وليس هذا بمقتض أن الإرادة تعلقت بخلق السماء بعد تمام خلق الأرض ولا مقتضيا أن خلق السماء وقع بعد خلق الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r3.claim: Istawa means directing oneself straight toward something without an intervening obstacle; here it represents God's will attaching to the creation of the heavens.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r3.anchor: والاستواء : القصد إلى الشيء توا لا يعترضه شيء آخر . وهو تمثيل لتعلق إرادة الله تعالى بإيجاد السماوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r4.claim: The wording may indicate one initial divine intention to create heaven and earth, whose effective execution was ordered first toward heaven and then toward earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r4.anchor: توجهت إرادته لخلق السماوات والأرض توجها واحدا ثم اختلف زمن الإرادة التنجيزي بتحقيق ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r5.claim: The imperative is a command of bringing into existence and supports reading the wording as describing God's effective will to create.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r6.claim: Dukhan is what rises from fuel when fire burns; describing heaven as smoke is an emphatic simile, meaning it was like smoke.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r6.anchor: والدخان : ما يتصاعد من الوقود عند التهاب النار فيه . وقوله : { وهي دخان } تشبيه بليغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r7.claim: A Prophetic report says heaven was ʿamaʾ, which Ibn ʿAshur explains as a thin cloud or fine moisture.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r7.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه لم يكن في الوجود من الحوداث إلا العماء ، والعماء : سحاب رقيق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r8.claim: One interpretation takes smoke to mean a dark substance, matching Genesis's statement that darkness was over the deep.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r8.anchor: وقيل : أراد بالدخان هنا شيئا مظلما ، وهو الموافق لما في ( سفر التكوين ) من قولها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAshur rejects the darkness interpretation as distant from the Prophetic account that the primordial ʿamaʾ existed before other created events.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r9.anchor: وهو بعيد عن قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه لم يكن في الوجود من الحوداث إلا العماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r10.claim: He understands ʿamaʾ as an approximation of the fine primordial substance from which beings were made; heaven formed from this smoke-like matter before earth existed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p245/r10.anchor: وهو تقريب للعنصر الأصلي الذي خلق الله منه الموجودات ، وهو الذي يناسب كون السماء مخلوقة قبل الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r1.claim: The creative address is directed to heaven and earth together before either existed; the command concerns God's power acting on their formative material, the smoke.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r1.anchor: أي قبل خلق السماء لا محالة وقبل خلق الأرض ، لأنه جعل القول لها مقارنا القول للسماء ، وهو قول تكوين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAshur relays a cosmological account in which some ʿamaʾ solidified into heaven, water formed with it, and earth arose by drying within that water, as in Genesis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r2.anchor: لأن السماء تكونت من العماء بجمود شيء منه سمي جلدا فكانت منه السماء وتكون مع السماء الماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r3.claim: Ityan literally means coming or approaching, but that sense cannot apply to heaven and earth here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r3.anchor: والإتيان في قوله : { ائتيا } أصله : المجيء والإقبال ولما كان معناه الحقيقي غير مراد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r4.claim: Heaven and earth are not rational beings with choice, and imagining God coercing them would imply that they initially lay outside His power; the literal reading must therefore be set aside.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r4.anchor: ولا يتصور منهما طواعية أو كراهية إذ ليستا من أهل العقول والإدراكات ، ولا يتصور أن الله يكرههما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r5.claim: On the first rhetorical reading, coming is a metaphor for accepting creation, just as turning away or fleeing can represent disobedience; the command means to comply with creative formation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r5.anchor: أن يكون الإتيان مستعارا لقبول التكوين كما استعير للعصيان الإدبار في قوله تعالى : { ثم أدبر يسعى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r6.claim: As an example of turning away as disobedience, the Prophet told Musaylima, who had refused faith and obedience, that if he turned away God would strike him down.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r6.anchor: وقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمسيلمة حين امتنع من الإيمان والطاعة في وفد قومه بني حنيفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r7.claim: On this first reading, the utterance itself is a metaphor for God's power attaching to what He brings about, as in His saying Be, and it is.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p246/r7.anchor: والقول على هذا الوجه مستعار لتعلق القدرة بالمقدور كما في قوله : { أن يقول له كن فيكون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r1.claim: Willingly or unwillingly is a metonymy for the unavoidable acceptance of the command, portraying God's power to create both realms as He wills; the phrase functions proverbially.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r1.anchor: كناية عن عدم البد من قبول الأمر وهو تمثيل لتمكن القدرة من إيجادهما على وفق إرادة الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r2.claim: The two verbal nouns are accusative circumstantial expressions modifying the pronoun in ītia: coming willingly or reluctantly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r2.anchor: مصدران وقعا حالين من ضمير { ائتنا } أي طائعين أو كارهين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r3.claim: A second reading treats the whole scene as a representation of God's power forming heaven and earth, pictured as an obedient servant ordered to a difficult task, with no actual speaker or spoken words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r3.anchor: مستعملة تمثيلا لهيئة تعلق قدرة الله تعالى لتكوين السماء والأرض لعظمة خلقهما بهيئة صدور الأمر من آمر مطاع للعبد المأذون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r4.claim: In the composite representation, willingly or unwillingly belongs to the depicted scene and has no counterpart in the state being represented; both readings emphasize the reach of divine power over all things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r4.anchor: والمقصود على كلا الاعتبارين تصوير عظمة القدرة الإلهية ونفوذها في المقدورات دقت أو جلت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r5.claim: The reported speech may personify the swift formation of heaven and earth as the prompt obedience of a willing servant, through implied metaphor and imaginative elaboration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r5.anchor: مستعارا لدلالة سرعة تكونهما لشبههما بسرعة امتثال المأمور المطيع عن طواعية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r6.speaker: الراجز الذي لا يعرف تعيينه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r6.claim: An unattributed rajaz line supplies an analogy for an inanimate thing being made to speak: the filled basin says enough.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r6.anchor: من باب قول الراجز الذي لا يعرف تعيينه : امتلأ الحوض وقال قطني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r7.claim: Alternatively, their speech depicts the formation of heaven and earth as the rapid, willing acceptance of an order; here the individual words are literal within a metaphorical composition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تمثيلا لهيئة تكون السماء والأرض عند تعلق قدرة الله تعالى بتكوينهما بهيئة المأمور بعمل تقبله سريعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r8.claim: The readings are close, but in the first speech, coming, and willingness are individual tropes; in the second, only the combined construction is figurative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r8.anchor: إلا أن القول ، والإتيان ، والطوع ، على الاعتبار الأول تكون مجازات ، وعلى الاعتبار الثاني تكون حقائق وإنما المجاز في التركيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r9.claim: The plural form is used because heaven comprises seven heavens, so the obedience comes from a plurality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r9.anchor: وإنما جاء قوله : { طآئعين } بصيغة الجمع لأن لفظ السماء يشتمل على سبع سماوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r10.claim: The masculine plural is appropriate because heaven and earth have no true grammatical sex.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p247/r10.anchor: وأما كونه بصيغة جمع المذكر فلأن السماء والأرض ليس لهما تأنيث حقيقي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p248/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p248/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p248/r1.claim: Using a rational masculine plural further reinforces the personification; the similar plural in the vision of eleven stars, sun, and moon is cited as a parallel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p248/r1.anchor: كونه بصيغة جمع العقلاء فذلك ترشيح للمكنية المتقدمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r1.claim: Istiwāʾ toward heaven means turning by God’s power and creation to bring the heaven into existence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r1.anchor: استوى إلى السماء معناه بقدرته واختراعه أي إلى خلق السماء وإيجادها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r2.claim: Reports describe the heaven as a soft body like smoke or vapor, or as something God commanded to rise from water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r2.anchor: روي أنها كانت جسما رخوا كالدخان أو البخار، وروي أنه مما أمره الله أن يصعد من الماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r3.claim: An unstated step is understood: God created, perfected, and completed the heaven before commanding heaven and earth to come.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r3.anchor: وهنا لفظ متروك ويدل عليه الظاهر، وتقديره: فأوجدها وأتقنها وأكمل أمرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r4.claim: The majority read it from atā, “come,” so the response means that the two came in obedience as God wished.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «إيتيا» من أتى يأتي «قالتا أتينا» على وزن فعلنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Mujahid read it from ātā, “give”: heaven and earth give the obedience God wants from them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن جبير ومجاهد: «آتيا» من آتى يؤتى «قالتا آتينا» على وزن أفعلنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r6.claim: Both readings indicate God’s subjection of heaven and earth and the functions he decreed for them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r6.anchor: والإشارة بهذا كله إلى تسخيره وما قدره الله من أعمالها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r7.claim: The phrase is elliptical: come willingly, or else you will be brought unwillingly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r7.anchor: وقوله: أو كرها فيه محذوف ومقتضب، والتقدير: ائتيا طوعا وإلا أتيتما كرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r8.claim: Qālatā refers to the two divisions, heaven and earth, treating the plural heavens and earths as two collectives.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r8.anchor: وقوله: قالتا أراد الفرقتين المذكورتين، وجعل السماوات سماء والأرضين أرضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r9.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r9.claim: The cited line describes two sets of ropes and two people’s groups as separate pairs, illustrating the dual expression.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r9.anchor: ألم يحزنك أن حبال قومي ... وقومك قد تباينتا انقطاعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r10.claim: One group holds that heaven and earth literally spoke after God gave them life and the capacity for speech; Ibn Atiyya prefers this as unobjectionable and a fuller display of divine power.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r10.anchor: فقالت فرقة: نطقت حقيقة، وجعل الله تعالى لها حياة وإدراكا يقتضي نطقها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r11.claim: Another group takes their reply figuratively as a visible choice of obedience and humility; Ibn Atiyya prefers literal speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r11.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هذا مجاز، وإنما المعنى أنها ظهر منها من اختيار الطاعة والخضوع والتذلل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r12.claim: The masculine rational plural follows the personification of the speakers as rational beings, as in the description of Joseph’s family in 12:4.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p6#2/r12.anchor: وقوله: طائعين لما كانت ممن يقول وهي حالة عقل جرى الضمير في طائعين ذلك المجرى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi refers back to his explanation of “then He turned to the heaven” at 2:29.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ثم استوى إلى السماء ﴾ قد شرحناه في البقرة 29

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r2.claim: One account says God sent wind over the water after creating it, raising smoke that became the heaven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنه لما خلق الماء أرسل عليه الريح فثار منه دخان فارتفع وسما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r3.claim: A second account says smoke rose from fire sent upon the earth after its creation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه لما خلق الأرض أرسل عليها نارا فارتفع منها دخان فسما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God told the heaven to reveal its sun, moon, and stars, and the earth to open its rivers and produce its fruits.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس قال للسماء أظهري شمسك وقمرك ونجومك وقال للأرض شققي أنهارك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses ṭāʾiʿīn as a circumstantial accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج هو منصوب على الحال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the masculine plural treats heaven and earth as rational, discerning beings, as at 36:40.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r6.anchor: وإنما لم يقل طائعات لأنهن جرين مجرى ما يعقل ويميز

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r7.claim: Another explanation is that they came obedient, along with whoever was within them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p245/r7.anchor: وقد قيل أتينا نحن ومن فينا طائعين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p165/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p165/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p165/r2.claim: This passage details the six-day creation: Earth was created first as the foundation before Heaven, while its later dahw means bringing out water and pasture after Heaven was created.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p165/r2.anchor: فذكر أنه خلق الأرض أولا لأنها كالأساس، والأصل أن يبدأ بالأساس، ثم بعده بالسقف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p165/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p165/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p165/r3.claim: A man asked Ibn ʿAbbās about apparent tensions in verses on mutual questioning, concealing polytheism, the order of Earth's and Heaven's creation, and descriptions of God's attributes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p165/r3.anchor: وقال المنهال، عن سعيد بن جبير قال: قال رجل لابن عباس: إني أجد في القرآن أشياء تختلف علي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r1.claim: The smoke is water vapor rising from the Earth as it was created.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r1.anchor: وهو: بخار الماء المتصاعد منه حين خلقت الأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r2.claim: God commanded Heaven and Earth to obey His command and respond to His act, willingly or under compulsion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r2.anchor: أي: استجيبا لأمري، وانفعلا لفعلي طائعتين أو مكرهتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God commanded the skies to bring out the sun, moon, and stars and the Earth to open rivers and produce fruits; they answered obediently.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله [تعالى] (1) {فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r4.claim: Their response means they submit with all they contain, ready for the angels, humans, and jinn God intends to create; Ibn Jarīr preferred Ibn ʿAbbās's reported explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r4.anchor: بل نستجيب لك مطيعين بما فينا، مما تريد خلقه من الملائكة والإنس والجن جميعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r5.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r5.claim: A view Ibn Jarīr quotes from an Arab grammarian treats the two as rational speakers by representing them as speaking.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r5.anchor: حكاه ابن جرير عن بعض أهل العربية قال: وقيل: تنزيلا لهن معاملة من يعقل بكلامهما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r6.claim: An unspecified view says the Earth speaker was the place of the Kaʿbah and the Heaven speaker was the corresponding place above it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r6.anchor: وقيل (3) إن المتكلم من الأرض بذلك هو مكان الكعبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r7.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī says that if Heaven and Earth had refused God's command, He would have punished them with pain; Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p166#2/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: لو أبيا عليه أمره لعذبهما عذابا يجدان ألمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p168/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p168/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p168/r1.claim: Abū Hurayrah attributes to the Prophet a creation sequence: soil Saturday, mountains Sunday, trees Monday, hardships Tuesday, light Wednesday, animals Thursday, and Adam late Friday; Muslim and al-Nasāʾī transmit it, though Ibn Kathīr calls it unusual among Ṣaḥīḥ reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p168/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيدي فقال: "خلق الله التربة يوم السبت، وخلق فيها الجبال يوم الأحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p168/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p168/r2.speaker: البخاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p168/r2.claim: Al-Bukhārī criticizes the report's attribution to the Prophet, saying the more accurate version has Abū Hurayrah transmit it from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p168/r2.anchor: وقد علله البخاري في التاريخ فقال: رواه بعضهم عن أبي هريرة [رضي الله عنه] (3) عن كعب الأحبار، وهو الأصح

JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r20.claim: Istawā ilā al-samāʾ means God turned toward creating the heaven.
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r20.anchor: (ثم استوى إلى السماء) أي: قصد إلى خلق السماء

JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r21.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r21.claim: One explanation identifies the smoke as water vapor.

JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r22.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r22.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the smoke as vapor from the earth.
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r22.anchor: وقيل: كان بخار الأرض، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r23.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r23.claim: Al-Hasan explains istawā as God’s command applying to the heaven.
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r23.anchor: وقيل: استوى أمره إلى السماء، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r24.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r24.claim: The command means God brought the heaven and earth into being as intended, without difficulty or resistance.
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r24.anchor: أراد به أنه كونهما كما أراد، فكان من غير تعذر وامتناع

JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r25.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r25.claim: The address and answer are figurative, not literal speech: heaven and earth were nonexistent or inanimate.
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r25.anchor: ولم يكن هناك خطاب منه لهما، ولا جواب منهما؛ لأنهما كانا معدومين أو جمادين

JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r26.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r26.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r26.claim: Arab idiom addresses non-speaking things as if they spoke; this is clearer and more majestic, eloquent, and well-ordered.
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r26.anchor: وإنما قيل ذلك؛ لأنه أبلغ في الإفهام والتعظيم، وأفصح في اللفظ، وأحسن في النظم

JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r27.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r27.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r27.claim: Jishumi illustrates figurative speech with examples of a full basin saying it has had enough and a traveler’s eyes answering obedience.
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r27.anchor: ومثل ذلك كثير في كلام العرب، كقول الحكيم: سل الأرض من شق أنهارك، وغرس أشجارك

JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r29.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r29.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r29.claim: A Prophetic report says God created earth on Sunday and Monday, mountains on Tuesday, and vegetation, water, settlements, and wasteland on Wednesday.
JISHUMI:v9p6172#2/r29.anchor: وفي خبر مرفوع: إن الله تعالى خلق الأرض يوم الأحد والاثنين، وخلق الجبال يوم الثلاثاء، وخلق يوم الأربعاء الشجر والماء والعمران والخراب

JISHUMI:v1p564/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p564/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p564/r21.claim: He cites the heavens' and earth's response as a parallel example of figurative “saying” in explaining “Be, and it is.”

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r4.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r4.claim: Ibn Isa glosses istawa ila as directed toward the heaven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r4.anchor: أحدهما : عمد إلى السماء , قاله ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r5.claim: Al-Hasan reads the phrase as God's command turning toward the heaven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r5.anchor: الثاني : استوى أمره إلى السماء , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r6.claim: The heaven is described as smoke when God turns toward it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r6.anchor: قوله عز وجل : { ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان } فيه وجهان :

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r7.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r7.claim: Ibn Bahr says the command came before creation: “Come” means “Be,” as in the command “Be, and it is” (16:40).
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r7.anchor: أحدهما : أنه قال ذلك قبل خلقها , ويكون معنى ائتيا أي كونا فكانتا كما قال تعالى { إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون } قاله ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r8.speaker: جمهور
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r8.claim: The majority say the command was addressed to heaven and earth after their creation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r8.anchor: الثاني : قول الجمهور أنه قال ذلك لهما بعد خلقهما .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r9.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr interprets the command as obeying the appointed course, willingly or under compulsion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r9.anchor: أحدها : معناه أعطيا الطاعة في السير المقدر لكما طوعا أو كرها أي اختيارا أو إجبارا قاله سعيد بن جبير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r10.claim: Another reading commands heaven and earth to come to God's worship and knowledge, willingly or unwillingly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r10.anchor: الثاني : ائتيا عبادتي ومعرفتي طوعا أو كرها باختيار أو غير اختيار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r11.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r11.claim: Al-Naqqash says the two were commanded to bring forth what was within them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r11.anchor: الثالث : ائتيا بما فيكما طوعا أو كرها , حكاه النقاش .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r12.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r12.claim: Ibn Bahr interprets the command as becoming as decreed: hard or soft, rough or smooth, inaccessible or accessible.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r12.anchor: الرابع : كونا كما أمرت من شدة ولين , وحزن وسهل ومنيع وممكن , قاله ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r13.claim: The address may have been spoken aloud, or manifested divine power may have conveyed the intended meaning in place of speech.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r13.anchor: وفي قوله { لها } وجهان : أحدهما : أنه قول تكلم به . الثاني : أنها قدرة منه ظهرت لهما فقام مقام الكلام في بلوغ المراد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r14.speaker: طاووس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r14.claim: Tawus transmits that the two answered, “We give obedience.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r14.anchor: أحدها : معناه أعطينا الطاعة , رواه طاووس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas says heaven brought its sun, moon, and stars, while earth brought trees, rivers, and fruits.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r15.anchor: الثاني : أتينا بما فينا . قال ابن عباس : أتت السماء بما فيها من الشمس والقمر والنجوم , وأتت الأرض بما فيها من الأشجار والأنهار والثمار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r16.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r16.claim: Ibn Bahr explains their answer as becoming what God wished them to be.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r16.anchor: الثالث : معناه كما أراد الله أن نكون , قاله ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r17.claim: Their obedience may have appeared in a way that stood for speech, or the two may literally have spoken.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r17.anchor: ظهور الطاعة منهما قائم مقام قولهما

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r18.speaker: أبو النصر السكسكي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r18.claim: Abu al-Nasr al-Saksaki says the Kaaba's site on earth and the corresponding site in heaven spoke, and God established His sanctuary there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p171/r18.anchor: قال أبو النصر السكسكي : فنطق من الأرض موضع الكعبة ونطق من السماء ما بحيالها فوضع الله فيها حرمه .

MUQATIL:41:9-11/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r6.claim: The heaven was smoke before this command was given.
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r6.anchor: { ثم استوى إلى السمآء وهي دخان } ، قبل ذلك

MUQATIL:41:9-11/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r7.claim: Before this command, God offered obedience with desires and pleasures in exchange for reward or punishment, but the heavens and earth refused out of fear.
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r7.anchor: عرض عليهما الطاعة بالشهوات واللذات، على الثواب والعقاب، فأبين أن يحملنها من المخافة

MUQATIL:41:9-11/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r8.claim: The command then called them to know their Lord and remember Him, giving obedience willingly or unwillingly without reward or punishment.
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r8.anchor: ائتيا المعرفة لربكما والذكر له، على غير ثواب ولا عقاب، طوعا أو كرها

MUQATIL:41:9-11/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r9.claim: They answered by giving God their obedience willingly.
MUQATIL:41:9-11/r9.anchor: { قالتآ أتينا طآئعين } [آية: 11]، يعني أعطيناه طائعين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r1.claim: Nasafi takes “turned toward heaven” metaphorically: Allah brought heaven into existence as He willed; the Arabic idiom means finishing one task and beginning another.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r1.anchor: هو مجاز عن ايجاد الله تعالى السماء على ما اراد تقول العرب فعل فلان كذا ثم استوى إلى عمل كذا يريدون انه اكمل الاول وابتدا الثاني

NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for heaven being created after earth, and for a cosmogony in which an enormous jewel melted, its smoke rose to become heaven, and its foam became earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r2.anchor: وبه قال ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما وعنه انه قال اول ما خلق الله تعالى جوهرة طولها وعرضها مسيرة الف سنة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r3.claim: The command to heaven and earth means Allah willed them into being; they could not resist and came to exist as He intended, like obedient recipients of a command.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r3.anchor: ومعنى امر السماء والأرض بالاتيان وامتثالهما اليه اراد ان يكونهما فلم يمتنعا عليه ووجدنا كما ارادهما وكانتا في ذلك كالمأمور المطيع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r4.claim: Earth was created as a body before heaven but spread out afterward, as 79:30 says; the command means each should assume its proper form: earth spread as a resting place and heaven as a roof.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r4.anchor: والأرض مخلوقة قبل السماء بيومين لانه قد خلق جرم الأرض اولا غير مدحوة ثم دحاها بعد خلق السماء كما قال والأرض بعد ذلك دحاها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r5.claim: Coming means coming into existence or occurrence, as when one says that a deed came out pleasing.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r5.anchor: ومعنى الاتيان الحصول والوقوع كما تقول اتى عمله مرضيا وقوله طوعا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r6.claim: “Willingly or unwillingly” shows the force of Allah's power and the impossibility of resistance, like telling a subordinate to act whether willing or not.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r6.anchor: وقوله طوعا أو كرها لبيان تأثير قدرته فيهما وان امتناعهما من تاثير قدرته محال كما تقول لمن تحت يدك لتفعلن هذا شئت أو ابيت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r7.claim: The accusative “طوعا أو كرها” marks a state; “طائعين” is masculine plural instead of feminine dual/plural because the two are addressed and described as willing or compelled, as with “prostrating.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p85/r7.anchor: ونتصابها على الحال بمعنى طائعتين أو مكرهتين وانما لم يقل طائعتين على اللفظ أو طائعات على المعنى لانهما سموات وارضون

QURTUBI-FULL:41:9-12/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:9-12/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:9-12/r20.claim: Turning to the sky means directing Himself to create and shape it.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:9-12/r20.anchor: أي عمد إلى خلقها وقصد لتسويتها

QURTUBI-FULL:41:9-12/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:9-12/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:9-12/r21.claim: Most views treat istiwa as an attribute of action, and al-Qurtubi begins to support this with a verse about forming the heavens.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:9-12/r21.anchor: والاستواء من صفة الأفعال على أكثر الأقوال يدل عليه قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi cites God's forming the sky into seven heavens as support for the preceding view that istiwa is an attribute of action.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r1.anchor: ثم استوى إلى السماء فسواهن سبع سماوات

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r2.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn Abbas that God's command ascended to heaven; al-Hasan also held this interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r2.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس في قوله: { ثم استوى إلى السماء } يعني صعد أمره

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r3.speaker: من قال إنه صفة ذاتية زائدة
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r3.claim: Those who treat istiwa as an additional essential attribute say God possessed it eternally with His attributes.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r3.anchor: ومن قال: إنه صفة ذاتية زائدة قال: استوى في الأزل بصفاته

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r4.claim: Thumma marks the sky's transition from smoke to density; the smoke came from water's breathing, as discussed in al-Baqara from Ibn Masʿud and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r4.anchor: و«ثم» ترجع إلى نقل السماء من صفة الدخان إلى حالة الكثافة

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r5.claim: The command means bring out benefits and goods placed in sky and earth for God's creatures.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r5.anchor: أي جيئا بما خلقت فيكما من المنافع والمصالح

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says God told the sky to bring out sun, moon, stars, winds, and clouds, and the earth to open rivers and produce trees and fruits.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قال الله تعالى للسماء: أطلعي شمسك وقمرك

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r7.claim: The reply omits words: they came to God's command willingly.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r7.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف أي أتينا أمرك

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r8.claim: One view takes the command as subjection, like God's word to a thing He wills; on that view it preceded creation, unlike the majority's post-creation view.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r8.anchor: وقيل: معنى هذا الأمر التسخير أي كونا فكانتا

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r9.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r9.claim: Al-Mawardi gives two views: God uttered speech to them, or a power appeared in them and served as speech to convey His intent.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r9.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى لهما وجهان: أحدهما أنه قول تكلم به

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r10.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r10.claim: Most scholars say God created speech in sky and earth, and they spoke as He willed.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r10.anchor: وقال أكثر أهل العلم: بل خلق الله فيهما الكلام فتكلمتا

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r11.claim: Another view says their visible compliance stood in place of speech, like a brimming basin said it was full.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r11.anchor: أحدهما أنه ظهور الطاعة منهما حيث انقادا وأجابا

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r12.speaker: الراجز
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r12.claim: A rajaz line about a basin saying it is full shows how an object's state may speak figuratively.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r12.anchor: ومنه قول الراجز: امتلأ الحوض وقال قطني

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r13.speaker: أبو نصر السكسكي
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r13.claim: Al-Saksaki says the Kaaba's site spoke from the earth, and the matching spot in heaven spoke; God then placed His sacred precinct there.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r13.anchor: قال أبو نصر السكسكي: فنطق من الأرض موضع الكعبة

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r14.claim: The masculine plural ṭāʾiʿīn is used although the pair is heaven and earth because the wording refers also to their inhabitants.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r15.claim: Another explanation says their speech and response make sky and earth grammatically like rational beings.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11/r15.anchor: وقيل: لما وصفهن بالقول والإجابة وذلك من صفات من يعقل

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r1.speaker: موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r1.claim: A report from al-Thaʿlabi says Moses asked what God would do if heaven and earth disobeyed; God said a creature would swallow them, located in one of His meadows, itself within His knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r1.anchor: وفي حديث: إن موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام قال: يا رب

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r2.claim: These authorities read ātayā with a long alif and fatḥ; the response ātaynā means give obedience and we gave it.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة «آتيا»

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r3.claim: On the reading meaning 'we gave obedience,' both objects are omitted; preferably it is a reciprocal verb with one object omitted.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r4.claim: Another reading of ātaynā means they came bringing what was within them, as explained elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:11-12/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ «آتينا» فالمعنى جئنا بما فينا
